statement: Plain words: click selects a building and the plan panel lists its rooms (at town/district zoom the click first opens the district detail); double-click or Show plan zooms until the floor plan is readable one storey at a time: rooms, walls, doors, windows, stairs, fireplaces with chimneys, simple furniture, a name per room; plan outer walls = house walls, windows on facade rhythm and dormers, stairs aligned cellar to attic, chimneys exit roof at fireplaces, front door = street door under its porch.

Plain words: programme first (what the building must hold: forge, common room, nave/chancel/crypt, one home per household) then walls; holdings grow with quarter wealth; a poor quarter re-cuts a rich house into lodgings off a corridor reached through a shared stair hall, never through a neighbour's rooms, nobody left out; multi-structure buildings give each structure its rooms; split brewer gets brewhouse in one and taproom in the other.

Plain words: ways down drawn in the plan (cellar stair to sewer, chapel stair to catacomb, crypt door/stair to catacomb, dug shaft, well breaking into a chamber) with what they reach and how they came to be; secret way down sits in its own hidden back room; cathedral always has a crypt, the town's largest (raised crypt under a raised choir on wet ground, entered from nave, stairs up to choir either side); other churches by row and ground; underground homes have no windows or chimneys, lamps and air-shaft venting or brazier.

Plain words: stepped/hillside buildings planned as they stand (tiers with own storeys at true heights, one stair carried up as many tiers as fits, landing doors, terraces with parapets exported as floor, lower-tier chimneys rising through tiers above); stepped temple = solid masonry with one sanctuary on top reached by the great stair, crypt below entered by a door at the platform foot (bare platform: plan is the crypt only; via annex cellar where an annex stands; raised annex on wet ground); solid monument way down = small door in its foot; retaining-wall house has no openings into earth; terrace-edge house gets a street-below walk-out cellar; back door may be one floor up; downhill-street house keeps front door on ground floor up outside steps with cellar door under/beside; church on slope may open a cellar beside its crypt to outside, never the crypt; deck buildings have no cellar or well over water and fall with the deck; arch workshop door/windows in the arch infill; aqueduct end house holds its tank; arena planned as ring of passages and stairs round its open floor.

Plain words: on change (sim moves a family, dossier turns a house into a shop) the plan is marked changed and waits until viewed, then changes as little as it can, never re-rolled; every element editable (rename, number rooms, add room, move wall, split/merge, move door/window/stairs/fireplace, furniture, light off, reassign household); a non-exact edit is done the nearest working way with a one-line report; every edit undoable and none reaches outside the building except a cellar edit opening/sealing a way underground, which warns first; each storey exports as a VTT scene with walls, doors, windows, lights.

At every level a row whose for.era is e wins over the era-less row at the same key (J-V3.78).

A1 main slot resolves by first match: (1) class-id row whose for.use is Use.specialisation under k, else under '*'; (2) class-id row for.cls = k, no for.use; (3) where h is not both and the row reached has no half cells, or no row reached: family row of V11 split.works or split.shop for k (by h); otherwise family row of k's templateFamily (v. key: row its V02 composition.classFamily key names, reported via); (4) building-class row of §2.6 Building.class; (5) fallback house class row when the building houses a household, else warehouse. Another slot resolves by 2.4's slot-row order. A row's room with half other than both and h is dropped. No use and no household -> vacant programme. Row, level, slot, half, era, vacant -> PlanReport.programmeSource. A concealed use resolves its own row by the same rule for A2 (6).

Band cells: authored four-column cell reads poor/modest/prosperous/rich (squalid = poor, comfortable = modest); continuous cells (areas, sizeFactor, furnish.density) interpolate linearly along the field value between the centres of the two bands it lies between (§4.5 centres); discrete cells switch at the cut.

Pattern precedence: at a band whose ladder form is lodging, apartment or room, the ladder row's circulation.patterns replace the resolved row's upper and top cells (first listed weight 2, each other weight 1); the resolved row governs every other cell.

A2 lists: ProgramRooms built in order (1)-(7), (9), (10), (11); (8) runs after A6; each carries origin, rule (row index in that list), scope, priority, and the resolved row's cells overriding the role table's.

A2 (1) units: per household in address order, its unit's rooms at the ladder row's form (scope unit, hard, origin ladder); unitOneRoom: one room of role room whose area triple is the sum of the form's unit-room triples; unitHearth false: cooking place carries no hearth (H1 skips). (1') live-in household (Building.dwelling, §4.7 S10b; J-V3.32): form = ladder form capped at dwelling, rooms marked liveIn for A5 (a). (2) shared rooms: ladder row's shared roles the resolved row's shared cell admits, scope shared, soft, origin ladder.

A2 (3) staff rooms of the owners' unit (form house or dwelling whose principal chamber is largest; ties by household address) by ladder staff.count: const n rooms or one per n principal chambers (chamber or solar rooms); area = sizeShare x target of the owners' principal chamber (largest chamber, solar or hall); service, soft, origin staff. (3b) workplace sleep-in: beds = ceil(workers.max x staffSleepIn), workers from V11 BuildingClassRow.staff at band b; beds >= 3 -> dormitory x ceil(beds/8); beds 1-2 -> staff chamber x beds; soft, origin sleepIn, storey rule top then upper; a journeymen slot's slot row holds the dormitory instead.

A2 (4) class and use rooms at band b, half-filtered, origin programme (vacant: vacant). A dwelling row's own rooms need form house: for dwelling rows (class house, cottage, row_house, manor; families dwelling-row, dwelling-detached, dwelling-compound, farm; village v.yeoman_house, v.parsonage, v.manor_house, and v.cottage, v.hovel via class rows; every slot row taking one of them) own rooms apply only where the ladder form at band b is house; otherwise units (1) and shared (2) replace them, as V02's rooms rung withholds hall and chapel (V02 §3.8, J-V2.36), and fill still runs; every other row keeps its own rooms at every band. Count laws per §10.2: const, perHousehold, perStorey (one per storey the rule admits), perCapacity (named capacity summed over sub-locations / perRoom, rounded up; guest room 2, dormitory 8, cell 1 by default), perSubLocation; a fractional count draws once on plan.program.

A2 (5) sub-locations: per SubLocation in id order, keys = its tags in order then cap:+largest capacity key (ties leisure, tempResidential, guestWorker, studying, working); roles of the first key with a SubLocationRoleRow; hosted by the first (4) room in list order whose role is among them and whose hosted count < role hosts; else adds a ProgramRoom of the first mapped role (soft, origin subLocation); store only when no key maps (reported); A2 writes ProgramRoom.subLocation, P5 copies to Room.subLocation; a custom service inside its provider (item 104 (h)(5)) arrives as such a sub-location with SF tags.

A2 (6) concealed rooms: per concealed use in id order, rooms of its resolved row marked concealed (§10.2 RoomRuleRow.concealed); none marked -> back room x 1 (hard) and strongroom x 1 (soft, basement preferred where one exists); flagged concealed, scope service, origin concealed. (7) declared rooms: Building.declaredRooms in list order, role x count, hard, origin declared, storey = declared exact level where given else role's; scope role's.

A2 (9) crypt: exactly when Basement.crypt exists: crypt x 1, hard, storey -1, area its ring, origin crypt, whatever class, band or vacancy; where the rank capped it, undercroft x 1 as well (hard, storey -1, area the capped bays' ring, origin crypt, rule 1). (10) access host rooms: per hosted access whose host roles name no room of the lists above on the head's storey class: cellar (basement head) or store (ground head) at min area, hard, origin access; none for a head with storey null and none on a crypt-only basement (heads hosted in its undercroft or crypt; J-V3.119).

So the court keeps O1 (b)'s arches and T28-2's reach.

A2 (8) entrance anchors (after A5 and A6): per entrance in ordinal order whose storey is not null (a solid stack's main entrance opens nothing; S6's root landing door takes its place with that door's storey), the first ProgramRoom on the entrance's storey not already anchoring, whose role is in the EntranceAnchorRow list in list order, takes anchor.entrance (crossPassage resolved at the cut: to the cross-passage strip where drawn else next entry; firstGround; concealedFirst); a room anchors one entrance only unless two inward points fall in one seed piece; no candidate -> stair hall at min area added (circulation, hard, origin entrance); every fall reported in PlanReport.anchors.

A3 sizes: areaM2 = role triple (or resolved override) x ladder sizeFactor at the value; a ring role takes its ring's area as min, target, max. Unit floor: where the sum of a unit's targets < unitFloorM2 of its form, every unit room scaled by floor / sum (min, target, max together). Provenance of the floor and the room role's 9 m2: own, general historical knowledge, not corpus-witnessed (item 104 (f)); floor measured at P6 (2.4 measure line, T-V3-35 (i)-(ii)); room area on that line too (written at M2b by V12 default line, restated at P1), measured at P6, never tuned (capacity reads its min from M2b).

A4 storey capacities: cap(s) = area(pieces(s)) - sum fixed rings on s - circulation(s) in area2; fixed rings those of 3.1 step 2 (stacks subtracted when A5 (c) places them); circulation(s) = area(pieces(s)) x num/den of the resolved circulation cell (integers; A6's ring counts inside), at least one landing (landingCm x the core's flight width) on every storey the core serves above its first; the crypt's piece is outside cap(-1) (holds the crypt alone).

A5 (a) units first (F-PLAN tier 0; deterministic, no draw): a storey is claimed when a hard non-unit room of the resolved row has that storey class; a house unit takes every storey above the basement; dwelling units take whole storeys in address order from the lowest unclaimed storey up (one each where storeys >= units; else split by wing in key order where wings >= units; else side by side around a lobby, 3.5 lodgings); live-in unit takes the lowest storey above the use's hard rooms with capacity, spilling upward; with no upper storey stays on ground marked farFromEntrance; lodging/apartment/room units pack first-fit from the top storey down (poorest highest), perStorey(s) = floor(cap(s)/unitArea), falling to the next poorer form (tier 0) until every household fits; a claimed storey tried last in every rule; when even room does not fit the no-abort ladder runs (3.9).

A5 (b) hard non-unit rooms by storey rule: ground (level 0 = lowest storeyed level, V2C-61), top (highest storeyed level), basement (-1), upper (lowest storey above 0 with capacity), notBasement, any and belowTop (storey with most capacity left among admitted, ties lower), declared exact level; a room whose rule admits no storey the building has is dropped (soft, tier 0) or delivered by tier 5 (hard); on a building with no storeyed wing it is dropped, hard or soft, with no tier, information solidMonument, listed in PlanReport.owed with no tier (T28-1's exception as BCR-V3-14 words it); a shortfall runs ladder step (ii).

A5 (c) hearths first among the wings: every allocated room needing a hearth (H1) takes its wing now by (e); then H1-H3 place stacks and cap(s) of every storey a stack crosses falls by its ring. (d) soft rooms by priority then list order; staff rooms by ladder staff.placement in order (attic top storey; basement; service = storey holding a service or back wing, BCR-V2-01), never on a storey holding the owners' principal rooms while another allowed storey has capacity; sleep-in staff top then upper downward; other soft rooms onto allowed storey with most capacity left (ties lower); a soft room fitting nowhere dropped (tier 0, reported), the unit's hearth room never (falls with its form); a storey class whose only positive-weight pattern is nave holds one target per seed piece, soft non-anchored extras go to another storey with capacity in level order before 3.5's strips.

A5 (e) wing choice inside a storey, first rule that decides: (1) an anchor names the wing (entrance inward point, stack, core bay, access head, composer room); (2) hard adjacency: direct or corridor -> partner's wing; under -> storey below its target's, under it; to core -> core's wing; to entrance:main or entrance:yard -> wing holding that entrance; (3) concealed room -> concealed entrance's wing, else wing holding the use's service rooms; (4) farFromEntrance -> wing farthest from main entrance's inward point; (5) WingAffinityRow first wing role the storey has with capacity (part:<name> wing carrying that template part name); (6) wing piece with largest remaining area; ties by wing key.

A5 (f) fill: per storey in level order, while spare capacity >= smallest target of the resolved fill list, fill rooms added cycling the list at target (soft, origin fill); a fill room is scope unit of the storey's household where every unit room on that storey belongs to one household, else service; after the cut a piece above its role's max keeps it (oversize, reported), never split below a min. Output: per storey and wing piece, an ordered list of targets.

A6 shared access: after A5, when the building houses two or more units, a live-in unit, or any unit with no room on the main entrance's storey (Entrance.storey; on a solid stack the root landing door's, S6): one stair hall ProgramRoom (circulation, hard, origin sharedAccess, that storey, anchor.entrance = main ordinal); area counts inside circulation(s) (nothing re-allocated); cut first on its storey (3.5 step 0).

Anchors: each is a fixed ring (§3.4 fixed) or an opening position placed from candidates on the wing-local module in the wing's OBB frame (§2.6 step 4), filtered by exact containment in every seed piece it must lie in (§3.4), ordered by a score then by lowest-leftmost lattice point, first taken; no anchor reads a stream so a plan.layout re-roll keeps them all (§6.1); every candidate keeps minEdge (§3.4) from other anchors' rings and from seed sides it does not lie on.

Level reading: a wing reaches V02 storeyRange(b,w) (solid wing none; storeyed ground wing [0, floors-1]; storeyed wing on another from the level above the one it stands on); s0(w) first level; ground(b) is level 0 when some storeyed wing stands on no other wing (BaseWing.on absent), else absent (stack whose every ground wing is solid). Level 0 is the lowest storeyed level (V02 BCR-V2-33, Storey.level), so on a solid stack level 0 is the shrine floor 10-25 m up: every rule meaning the real ground reads ground(b), never storey 0 (W2 basement exposure, core join to basement and tomb door 3.7.1, heads' storey 3.7.2 (1), crypt stairs 3.7.6, crawl hatch 3.7.7, switcher names 4.5). A solid wing is never a seed piece, host room, affinity target or stair candidate's wing; a door in its outer face is an opening onto the ground, not a room. Where no wing stands on another, storeyRange is the base's reading and every rule unchanged (T-V3-34).

Storey heights and floor datums: storeyed wing w of n = heights.floors storeys has run E(w) = deckLevel(w) - heights.baseCm (V02 deckLevel: eave less a flat roof's parapet); nominal heights from V11 HeightsRow.storeyCm via the designation template's heights key: G = storeyCm.ground for the first storey (a stacked tier's first storey is a principal floor too, J-V2.85), U = storeyCm.upper for others (tower/turret wing: towerStoreyCm else U for all); scaled so h(w,0) = floor(ratio(E x G, G + (n-1) x U)), h(w,j) = floor(ratio(E x U, G + (n-1)U)) for 0<j<n-1, top takes the remainder (sum h = E exactly; one storey h = E); a class without a heights row: floor(ratio(E,n)) per storey, remainder on top. storeyCm(w,s) = h(w, s - s0(w)); floorCm(w,s) = baseCm + sum_{j<s-s0} h(w,j) for s >= s0(w); a stacked wing's baseCm is deckLevel of the wing it stands on (BCR-V2-32). For s < 0: baseCm of the ground wing above less abs(s) x cellar.depthCm; half basement: baseCm raised by cellar.depthCm/2 (V02 BCR-V2-28, J-V2.91), floor at datum less half depth; crypt-only half form: seed wings' only (cryptSeedWings(b)), choir flights (3.7.6 (c)) climb the difference; raised crypt floor is V02's (V2 §3.14.5 (d); inside a solid tier 0 V2C-68). Each seed piece keeps its wing's floorCm; a room's elevation is its wing's floorCm at its storey (exports read it).

S1 stair bay size: h = largest storeyCm(w,s) among storeys the core climbs from (basement: cellar.depthCm; chain: over every wing it serves); risers n = ceil(h/riserCm) (n = 0 allowed for a crypt entry at level: bay of landingCm depth); flight width f (house or institution by class); straight f x ((n-1) goingCm + landingCm); dogleg 2f x (ceil((n-1)/2) goingCm + landingCm); winder 2f x 2f; spiral the tower's round room or a spiralCm disc as a 16-gon on the lattice; ladder = ladder cm; trapdoor = hatchCm square. Defaults with a 300 cm storey: straight 90 x 412, dogleg 180 x 251, winder 180 x 180.

S2 stair candidates: every bay position on the module whose long side lies along a wing side (exterior, party, court) or a joint, inside the wing's seed piece at every storey the core serves (plus the basement ring where Basement.access is core and 3.7.1 lets the core join it; a chain core inside every served wing at every served level), never in a solid wing; excluded: a bay over the passage room, a composer room it cannot stand in (§2.6 contract), a head's ring, a crypt stair or choir flight, a column, an entrance's clearance square (door width square inward), a hearth apron.

S3 score by stair.placement: by_entrance = distance from the main entrance's inward point (opening midpoint moved door.mainCm inward); rear = distance to the wing side opposite the frontage (a court ring side for a ring wing of a closed court, arena included, V2C-59); centre = distance to centroid; tower = the tower's round room (spiral bay a sector against the wall, or whole room for a stair turret) else centre's order. Where A2 finds shared access likely (two or more households, a live-in, or a dwelling-or-poorer unit in a multi-storey building) every score adds the bay's distance from the main entrance's inward point.

S4 kind fallback: no candidate for the row's kind -> next kind of dogleg -> straight -> winder -> ladder from the row's kind onward, then trapdoor for the basement (§2.6 step 3); each fall an anchor tier 2; none left -> tier 6 (upper storeys unreached, building flagged, §5.2); flights drawn, not stored.

S5 cores: (a) chains of stacked storeyed wings first: a chain starts at a storeyed wing standing on no storeyed wing and continues level by level through the storeyed wing standing on the previous (V02 lays at most one storeyed tier on a tier, shrine last; a solid wing between ends the chain); a chain of two or more levels takes one core whose candidates lie inside every served wing at every served level; tries whole chain then each shorter prefix from its bottom, takes the longest prefix with a candidate, then S3's score; under V02's internal stair form (tiered tower) placement centre, kind spiral whatever the row says; a stacked wing the chain core does not reach takes its own core from s0(w) where it has two or more storeys, and is joined by S6 in any case; (b) joined wings along a joint of at least 2f share the core of the wing earliest in clip order when its bay lies within 2f of that joint, both reach its storeys and their floorCm at each shared storey differ by at most datum.maxSteps x riserCm; a tower serves the wing it joins (§2.6); (c) every other wing with upper storeys is reached by its own core.

S6 joining a stacked wing y on x (in key order): (a) landing door where stairChain(b) has a flight with to = x: one door of door.entranceCm on y's ring side landingSide(b,y) at level s0(y), centred on the side point nearest the midpoint of the flight's head side within access.snapCm, else side midpoint (reported landingDoor, tier 2, with distance), opening from the terrace into y's room; (b) terrace exit else, where no chain core serves y and a core serving x's top storey has its bay inside T(x)'s projection: that core's levels upper bound becomes s0(y), its bay at s0(y) a stair room on the terrace (stair house) with one open opening onto T(x), y's nearest room takes a terrace door (O1 (d)); reported terraceExit; (c) terrace door else, where a chain core serves y and T(x) is flat: y's room at s0(y) with the longest exterior run on T(x) takes one door of door.entranceCm onto it; reported terraceDoor; (d) seating exits: with seatingExits (arena), every core whose bay lies against a joint with a solid wing ends at its wing's top storey in one open opening onto the solid wing's roof (seating); reported seatingExit; (e) unreached: a y none of (a)-(c) and no core joins is F-PLAN tier 1, flagged W_TIER_UNREACHED (V2C-47 (2) sealed stair form none lands here by design).

Solid stack's root: where ground(b) is absent the main entrance stands where V02 BCR-V2-41 puts it (foot of the stair chain, or tier 0's front side on a sealed stack) and opens no plan door (Entrance.storey null); the plan's root is the landing door of the first storeyed wing the stair chain reaches in chain order (sealed stack has no chain: its storeyed wing falls to (e)); A2 (8) and A6 read that door and storey; every plan-side rule reading the main entrance's inward point (S3 scores, patterns' entrance requirement, cross_passage, A5 (e) (4), 3.5 step 0, O2) reads that door instead, while the tomb door (3.7.1) and the crypt's seed and growth (3.7.4) read the main entrance itself.

A building with no storeyed wing at all (solid monument, sealed stack whose every wing is solid, a great temple laid with top flat by V02's stepped-temple row or its tiers op V2 §3.15.4, §4.6) has no level at or above ground and no room there, reported solidMonument (no failure); its terraces and flights are V02's roofscape; basement storeys planned alone (non-stair-entered crypt entered from basementDoor(b) directly or through O2's one crypt join); without a basement its hosted accesses keep outside-door heads (storey null); with neither the plan is empty. A sealed stack carrying a storeyed tier or shrine is planned and flagged by (e).

H1 hearth demand: every allocated room whose role row or resolved cell sets hearth, and the unit's cooking room in every unit form that has one (unless unitHearth false), needs a hearth on a wall of that room.

H2 stack candidates (after A5 (c)), in the historical order of a town house, with one rule over the whole order: a candidate whose column lies inside the extent of a wing standing on the hearth's wing (directly or higher) is taken only after every candidate under the hearth wing's own exposed roof or terrace. (a) back to back: where one wing piece of a storey holds two hearth targets, a doubleCm stack centred on the lattice line across the piece's long axis at the two targets' area ratio measured from the end nearer the main entrance (no stream); if hall_and_parlour is drawn its cut is two splitFaces ending on the stack's ring, every other pattern cuts around it; (b) party wall; (c) gable (wing side at end of its ridge axis); (d) any exterior side; (e) joint side between wings, a smoke hood (reported hood); no candidate -> tier 6 (hearth omitted, room kept, reported). Many hearths in one piece (N > 2): m = ceil(N/2) doubleCm stacks against the side away from the frontage (else longest exterior side) at (i + 1/2) x L/m along it, each serving two units; each cooking place assigned to the part sharing a side with its stack. Stacks rise: a stack placed for a lower hearth is offered first to the same wing's hearth room on every higher storey.

H3 placement: ring stackCm (or doubleCm) against its wall at the module position nearest the wall midpoint (or position (a) or the pitch rule gives) keeping apronCm clear floor in front inside the piece; a fixed ring on every storey from lowest hearth to the top storey its wing reaches and on through every level of every storeyed wing whose extent contains the column (tiers of a stack), up to the highest; a solid wing over the column is masonry the flue passes with no ring cut; each crossed storey's seed piece opened with the ring and cap(s) reduced; the column is one point on all its storeys (§2.6 Chimney), no stack ends under a floor; a hearthless air stack carried the same way.

H4 records: one Chimney per stack (levels from lowest hearth to highest level H3 carried it to; wing = hearth's wing); Room.hearth = {wall, at, chimney} filled after the partition gives wall ids; a stack carried into another wing is reported stackCarried (information, no tier); the roofscape draws the stack over column on the roof or terrace at levels[1]'s wing, never on Chimney.wing's roof where a wing standing on it covers the column (V2 §5.2; V2C-55 (2)).

E1 entrance points: each entrance's inward point (opening midpoint moved door.mainCm inward) on its storey (Entrance.storey, BCR-V3-26); an entrance with storey null has none (S6 root); the piece holding it receives the entrance's anchored room (A2 (8)). E2 composer rooms and the passage room are fixed rings as §2.6 states (an omitted gate hall's ring laid here by A2 (11)); a composer room keeps its composer role.

Seed pieces per storey (§2.6 steps 1, 4): extents of the wings reaching the storey (V02 storeyRange; solid none), clipped by tileRings in clip order, span rings at the ground storey, Basement.ring below (storey -1 with the crypt ring cut out as its own piece and capped bays as another), opened with the fixed rings of 3.3 and 3.7 on one transient arena per storey; work limit = plan stage WorkLimitLaw row (plan.storey, moduleCells = sum piece area / moduleCm2, 40 per unit, floor 2000); storeys are exactly storeyRange's levels (ground wing: Heights.floors; an attic is a storey only where floors counts it, its rooms taking the top rule); a stacked wing's extent lies inside the wing it stands on (V2 §3.15.1 ST6) and the lower wing reaches nothing at its levels, so each tier's storeys are cut on its own extent.

Roof terraces: for every wing x whose own RoofSpec.kind is flat (laid: V02 MassingRef.stack.lowerRoof below the top tier, top flat or shrine; or set by an edit V2 §4.6 (3)), solid or storeyed: T(x) = ring(x) minus union ring(y) over wings y with y.on = x (stairs included; kernel exact difference on the lattice, may have several faces); floor deckLevel(x); edge along ring(x)'s sides carries V02 parapetCm (0 none); a pent roof makes no terrace; MassingRef.stack read only for the shrine identity. Level: T(x) belongs to level s0(y) of the storeyed y on x; with none, storeyRange(b,x)[1]+1 for a storeyed x (a roof level with no rooms); no level for a solid x nothing storeyed stands on (drawn as roof in the next storeyed level's scene, else roofscape alone). Walkable when a flight's head arrives (stairChain to = x), a terrace exit opens onto it, or a landing/terrace door opens onto it; else roof; on a solid stack only the terrace whose level holds the shrine floor is walkable in the shrine's scene. A roof level is exported as a scene only where a flight or terrace exit reaches it; the switcher lists it as Roof terrace. Outside ground for W2: a wall of y facing T(x) is deckLevel(x); facing a pent skirt, the skirt's height at the wall (ridge line), never walkable. Derived at every derivation and at read for a stored plan; nothing stored.

Step 0 shared-access strip (A6): on the main entrance's storey (or root landing door's), p = that door's inward point, B = bay of the core serving the most unit storeys (ties: nearest p): where B lies in p's seed piece within corridorCm + door.mainCm of the entrance's side, the stair hall is the wing-frame rectangle from that side to B's far side, width max(B's width along the side + corridorCm, door.mainCm + 2 jambCm), clipped to the piece and grown to the role's min area along the side; otherwise a strip corridorCm wide whose centreline runs from p along the entrance side's inward normal until it meets the line of B's nearest long side, then parallel to B (two or three segments on the module); where B lies in another piece the path runs to the nearest joint point and continues by the same rule; the strip is cut by splitFaces along its long edges (polylines of at most three vertices ending on piece boundary or fixed ring), takes the stair hall's target, and is the main entrance's anchored room. Fallback: if no strip leaves every remaining part >= minRoomWidthCm, S3 re-run with distance to p only and retried; failing that, a lobby of corridorCm x (door.mainCm + 2 jambCm) at the entrance and each unit reaches it by O5's strip (tier 2, reported sharedAccess).

Drawn pattern: plan.layout draws one pattern per storey class from the resolved weights (after A1's precedence); it applies to the seed piece holding its PatternRow requirement (entrance: piece holding main entrance's inward point; hall: piece holding a hall, common room or taproom target and one more; core: piece holding the core's bay else main entrance; courtOrStreet: piece with a court or frontage side; none: largest piece, ties by wing key); every other piece takes the first positive-weight pattern of its cell's list whose requirement it holds, else bisect; where no piece holds the drawn requirement every piece takes that rule and the fall is reported; Plan.pattern records the drawn pattern, PlanReport.patterns per-piece ones.

Cut machine slice(piece, axis, area2) in the wing's OBB frame: for module position t, L(t) perpendicular to axis; fill fixed-ring holes (stack, column, head) to get P-hat; maximal segments of L(t) intersect P-hat; candidate = segment containing the point nearest the piece's OBB centre, written as one splitFace per stretch outside the fixed rings (rings bridge, never cut), ends placed by §3.4's input-side rule; a position whose candidate does not split into exactly two faces has no cut; start-side part (lower t) exact area2 compared to target; bisection over module positions with a candidate (O(log cells)); when start-side area is not monotone across the bracket, linear scan bounded by the storey work limit. Refusals: part narrower (OBB short side) than target role's minWidthCm or minEdge refused, next position tried; part above aspectMax tried only after every position within it (soft). strip(piece, side, depth): band of depth along one side (splitFace parallel).

P0: while a piece has a re-entrant vertex and holds more than one target, cut from its first re-entrant vertex in lattice order along whichever OBB axis gives two parts whose area ratio is nearest the target groups' ratio (groups by bisect's split); the position is the vertex's, no search.

Assignment per cut, in order: anchored targets to the part holding their anchor (containing entrance inward point or head, or sharing a side with the anchor ring: stack, core bay, composer room); adjacency-hard pairs to parts sharing the cut; concealed targets to parts farthest from the hub (parts not adjacent to the main entrance's anchored piece first, then by distance from its inward point, larger first); farFromEntrance to the part farthest from that point; then largest target first to the larger part. Bias tie-break when both parts lie within a role's [min,max]: sun (hall, parlour, solar, common room, taproom, shop) takes the part whose exterior walls' outward normals come nearest the path sun's noon azimuth at the equinox for the recipe's latitude (§8.4 sampler, item 102 (a),(d)); lowEnd takes the part at V02 MassingRef.low end where recorded else the part whose centroid samples lowest; sunTieBreak false switches sun off; further ties lattice order; no room waits for a label (§2.6 step 4).

Patterns: nave (principal target, anchored else largest, takes the piece; other targets cut by strip along the side farthest from the main entrance's inward point in list order, depth = target area / side usable length floored at minWidthCm; a strip that would leave the principal below min is not cut, target dropped (soft, tier 0) or tier 5 (hard); a church whose chancel is not a wing part takes its chancel strip at the crypt ring's nave-side edge where it has a crypt, report noting over/undersize); bisect (P0; split targets into two nearest-equal-area groups largest-first greedy; slice across the longer OBB axis at the groups' ratio; recurse); follow (strip galleryCm along the court side else frontage side as gallery circulation; rest sliced across the long axis in order); spine (short side >= 2 minRoomWidthCm + corridorCm: corridor strip along the long axis from the core's bay to the far end, from a mid-length core to both ends, targets alternately either side, each side sliced; else single-loaded along the side away from frontage); hall_and_parlour (one slice at hall/(hall+parlour), around a back-to-back stack where H2 (a) placed one; remaining by bisect in the parlour end); cross_passage (strip crossPassageCm across the wing through the main entrance's inward point, reaching the opposite side and its rear/yard door; hall on the larger side, buttery/kitchen/store/shop sliced on the other); enfilade (slice across the long axis only, targets in list order; aligned doors O4); lodgings (dwelling lobby, A5 (a): lobby strip corridorCm x (corridorCm + door widths) at the main entrance or the A6 strip, then bisect into units, each unit's rooms by bisect: a variant of bisect, not an eighth LayoutPattern value). plan.layout also draws each tie between equal-score cut positions (3.10).

P5 read-back and walls: readBack (§3.4) gives faces; each takes its target's role, scope, unit, concealment and program index; faces without a target (slivers, strips) merge into the adjacent circulation face where one exists, else into the neighbour with least area over its target (absorbSliver or mergeFaces, never across a joint); walls are edges between different faces typed by §2.6 (exterior on a seed side facing outside, party on the plot's party-wall edge, court on a court ring, partition otherwise), collinear pieces merged between the same two faces; structural faces keep their structural roles. P6 units' inner rooms: inside a unit's piece its rooms cut by bisect, cooking place last, against the stack when the form has one.

P7 roles within exchange classes (plan.roles): the cut's assignment re-dealt inside each exchange class = the storey's non-anchored rooms (no entrance, hearth, core, head or composer anchor) of one scope, unit, maxDoors, hub-ness and door kind, where every member role's storey rule is met by every member's storey, every member piece's area lies in every member role's [min,max] and every member's OBB short side >= every member role's minWidthCm; plan.roles draws a permutation over pieces in piece order (Fisher-Yates on the stream, creation index 3.10); a roles re-roll moves no wall and no opening (T28-6, T-V3-19) and re-derives only windows, furniture, lit and labels (§6.1).

O1 candidate door edges: (a) every wall between two rooms of length >= door width (O3) + 2 jambCm; entrances fixed openings at their vertices (§2.6 rule 5), kind entrance; passage room's two passage openings fixed; (b) fixed arches: a gatehall room takes an arch of door.archCm centred on each wall on a court ring; the composed hall's court door (V2 §3.8 (1), where the main entrance is not on the main wing) is a fixed door of door.mainCm at V02's offset on the hall's court wall; both secondary roots; (c) floor datums: rooms whose floorCm differ by delta take a plain door where delta <= riserCm, a door with steps = ceil(delta/riserCm) treads inside the lower room (footprint kept free by F2) where delta <= datum.maxSteps x riserCm, no door otherwise (joinsRefused, reported); a church's nave and lifted chancel joined by choir flights instead; (d) stack joins: each landing door, terrace door and seating exit is a fixed opening of S6's width and a stack root; setOpening on an exterior wall lawful where the outside is a walkable terrace or ground within the datum tolerance, else bent to the nearest such wall of the same room, named; (e) main entrance stoop: where no level the main entrance may open on (over an external basement, levels at or above ground) meets the outside ground and its floor lies > riserCm above, the opening carries steps = ceil(delta/riserCm) treads outside the wall (inside the porch where one stands), uncapped; above datum.maxSteps reported stoop; a main entrance whose floor lies below the outside ground by more than the tolerance is reported joinsRefused and still opened (rule 5).

O2 the tree: Prim's algorithm over internal edges from the main entrance's room on its storey (solid stack: from S6's root landing door; no storeyed wing: from the basement root) until every room with an internal path is spanned; stack roots: each S6 landing door, terrace exit or terrace door whose room is unspanned starts a further Prim tree (same costs) in S6's order, reached via stairChain's exterior flights and walkable terraces (BCR-V3-14 extends T28-2); basement root: where Basement.access is external and basementDoor(b) not null, the storey -1 room its door opens into starts a further tree over basement storeys' internal edges after the stack roots (core stops at ground storey, §2.6 step 3; §2.6 step 5 as V02 BCR-V2-33 (c) words it; T28-2's external clause); on a building with no storeyed wing it is the first and only tree. Edge cost 1 into a circulation room, 2 between a hub and a room of its unit or use, 3 otherwise; soft adjacency pair one less (never below 1); hard direct adjacency pair is a forced edge taken first; ties by room index.

O2 forbidden edges: between rooms of two different units; between a unit room and a service room of the use (live-in unit excepted, by O4's loop only); between a concealed room and a public one; between the crypt and any other basement room but its capped bays' undercroft (3.7.5's arch, a forced edge); where the crypt is stair-entered, between that undercroft and any other basement room (vault closed to the rest of the basement; crypt entered from the church above); a crypt stair's foot and a head's bay are not such rooms; into a room already at its role's maxDoors.

O2 crypt join: on a building whose crypt is not stair-entered (entered from the basement, never from the church above), the tree spanning the basement (basement root's, else the main tree entering storey -1 by the core bay or trapdoor) joins the crypt to the rest of the basement by exactly one join within the crypt role's maxDoors: (i) tree enters outside the crypt: at the first spanned room adjoining the crypt while unspanned, 3.7.5's arch where that room is the undercroft, else one new arch of door.archCm on the shared wall, tree continuing from the crypt; (ii) tree enters in the crypt (outside door or core bay opens into it): 3.7.5's arch where the crypt has capped bays, else one new arch to the adjoining room of least edge cost (ties room index), tree continuing from that room; reported as a cryptStair anchor noted crypt join (3.9).

O2 secondary entrances (side, rear, yard, service incl. a walk-out low-side door; O1 (b) arches and court door) add their own openings only, never a tree edge; a room reachable only through one is tier 1, except a concealed suite with a concealed entrance, joined only through it. Structural faces: the core's bay on each storey it serves is a stair room joined by one open opening onto its adjacent circulation room else its largest neighbour (§2.6 step 5), on storey -1 never a room of a stair-entered crypt's closed vault; storeys linked through it (a portal in exports); crypt stair joins the nave; choir flight joins nave and chancel; a head's bay joins its host room by the head's opening, outside the host's maxDoors; stack, through-ring and column are outside the graph (BCR-V3-9); an unreached room is tier 1 (3.9).

O3 width, position, leaf and swing: widths main entrance door.mainCm; other entrances door.entranceCm; service-scope room to circulation or yard door.serviceCm; other doors door.internalCm; arch door.archCm; open doorway the whole wall where the wall is a pattern strip's side <= corridorCm + 2 jambCm, else door.archCm; heights door.heightCm; a door stands at jambCm + width/2 from the wall end nearer the tree parent's centroid, hinge at that end, swinging into the child room (into the unit from its corridor; into a room from the street), except where its swing square overlaps a stair bay, head, stack apron or another door's square: then other end, then wall midpoint, then other swing (deterministic); arches and open doorways at wall midpoint; door kind = child room's role door; a roles re-roll never changes kind, width or position.

O4 loops by rule, never by chance: hall-parlour and hall-stair hall where they share a wall; kitchen-its yard door's room; every consecutive enfilade pair (doors aligned on the line moduleCm in from the court or street side); common room-kitchen; live-in unit's hub-the use's principal room where they share a wall (the unit's entry stays on circulation); a loop never joins two units or a concealed room to a public one.

O5 unit entries: a unit's entry is the tree edge from its first room to circulation or the street (Plan.units[].entry); where none exists (pieces touch no circulation) its largest room nearest the core (or the A6 strip) gets a corridorCm circulation strip cut along its wall toward the core, the unit room keeping its role if its area stays >= min; else tier 1; this is how a subdivided shell grows its corridor.

O6 concealed openings: an opening is concealed exactly when a room on either side is concealed (derived); a concealed suite with a concealed entrance is joined through it; one without is joined by one concealed opening to one of the use's service rooms; a secret head's room is joined by one concealed opening to the cellar, or to the concealed suite where one lies on that storey (3.7.3).
W1 exterior demand per room: none 0; some one window per exterior wall holding at least one facade bay, at most 2; max one per facade bay.

Outside ground and exposure on every storey (item 110 (a)): for each exterior wall of every storey, outsideCm = the surface sampled door.mainCm outward along the outward normal from the wall midpoint: levelledGroundCm(doc, key, p) (BCR-V5-30: levelled platform datum else raster; key = the building's arena, ground or sky island), never a direct Terrain raster read; where the wall midpoint lies within cellar.insetCm + door.mainCm of a RetainingWall chain and the sample lies across it, levelledGroundCm on the chain's far side, never the blend across the step (V02 BCR-V2-42 wall-side datum); on a deck (bridge, pier, mole, quay) the deck's surfaceCm, over open water the water surface; inside the ring of another wing of the building that reaches no level there (the wing a stacked wing stands on, stair wing, solid seating bank) that wing's roof surface (terrace deckLevel, pent skirt, stair height); only a walkable terrace is walkable. With exposureAllStoreys (default true): a window stands only where floorCm(w,s) + window.sillCm >= outsideCm; a door or entrance opening only where abs(floorCm - outsideCm) <= datum.maxSteps x riserCm and the outside is walkable (ground, deck, walkable terrace; never water or pent roof), main entrance excepted (O1 (e)); a basement wall keeps the light rule, exposure read against the ground wing above; with it false, only the basement rule reads the outside (no-op pin, T-V3-34).

Entrance storeys: deriveEntrances (§2.6) writes each entrance's storey: the level (basement levels included) whose floorCm at the entrance's wing meets outsideCm at its vertex within datum.maxSteps x riserCm, nearest where two meet (a hill-town house entered from two streets has its back door one floor up; a walk-out's low-side side door opens into the cellar); the main entrance over an external basement reads levels at or above ground only (core stops at ground storey, §2.6 step 3; J-A29.25); a walk-out house fronting its street downhill keeps its main entrance on level 0 with its stoop, its basement entered at basementDoor(b) commonly on its low street side (rule 3); S11 derives entrance storeys after the basement decision and a change of the basement's access, kind or floors re-derives them; the storey step draws nothing, so door and basement draws keep their order on siteplan.entrance (J-A29.61); with no level meeting its ground a side, rear, yard or service entrance is not derived (dropped after its draws on siteplan.entrance; reported W_ENTRANCE_NO_STOREY) and the main entrance keeps level 0 with its stoop; ground(b) absent -> main entrance storey null; exposureAllStoreys false -> every storey 0 where ground(b) exists.

W2 bays: on every side of every wing, V02 facadeBays(wing, side, bayM) (V2 §3.7: eave side with its valley term, any other side of a rect or quad wing without it, a polygon wing's bays round its free perimeter), so plan windows, dormers and §8.4 lit windows share one rhythm; a side with no bay takes no window; bays identical on every storey so stacked windows align (§2.6 step 6); a window takes a bay centre moved along the wall to keep endClearCm from partitions, openings and stacks within its bay (no window where that fails); none on a party wall. Kinds: slit (slitCm) on above-ground walls of a tower, turret or keep wing; on a basement wall a light window only where exposure (baseCm of the ground wing above less its outsideCm) >= window.lightBelowCm (half cellar, walk-out low side and its retaining-wall face, raised crypt walls), none on a buried wall; window otherwise; every window also passes the exposure gate.

Under V03 §11's Q1 order (plan rung before V02's M6b), V02's facadeBays, endMarginM and bayM are built first as V02's own item, moved forward from its M6b and priced there, exported from @plat/plots as massStepped is; P1 imports them and prices none (S23-36).
W3 width by occupants' band (window.widthCm), ids by 2.2; the reference's window-density baseline is §13.5's descriptive row, never a rule.

W4 dormers (§2.6 step 6; V2 §3.7 precedence): a room under a terrace or flat roof takes no dormer; on a stack top storey = each storeyed wing's own top level under a pitched roof; V02 tier, shrine and stair roles admit no dormer row (V2 §3.15.3). With a composition: an unedited DormerRow's count = number of top-storey roofed rooms with exterior demand whose exterior wall lies under that eave, at most its nb; kind and widthCm kept, positions V02 dormerPositions; each such room takes the dormer in its bay as its window; an edited DormerRow (edited true) is a fixed input: each top-storey room under one of its dormers takes it as its window whatever its demand. Without a composition, Wing.dormers is that count (§2.6), derived.

Basement storey: storeys -1..-k cut like any storey on Basement.ring (seed), storey -1 less the crypt's piece and its capped bays' piece, with the core's bay where Basement.access is core; rooms are A5's basement allocation (cellar, store, undercroft service; a concealed use's strongroom; A2 (10) host rooms), with nothing allocated one cellar (nave); crypt is its own piece; access follows §2.6 step 3 (core, trapdoor, external with its door at basementDoor(b); BCR-V3-32); an access or basement change marks the rung stale (§2.8 inputs as BCR-V3-19 words them).

Where a core joins the basement: only where ground(b) exists and the core's wing stands on the ground and reaches level 0; its bay then inside the part of Basement.ring under a storeyed ground wing, else the base's trapdoor fallback in that part; in either case outside the vault of a stair-entered crypt; a crypt-only basement's cores are its crypt stairs; a building with a solid ground wing beside a storeyed one (arena seating beside its ring, stepped temple with storeyed annex) is joined so, never forced outside.

Walk-out at a retaining wall (item 110 (a)): where a footprint side lies on or within cellar.insetCm of a RetainingWall's high side whose step there is at least half the cellar depth, the basement decision takes the walk-out form (Basement.access external), outside door on that side onto the lower terrace by basementDoor(b) rule 1; W2 gives that face light windows; V02 keeps buildings off a wall by template setback (V2 §3.17 (a)), so it fires where the setback < cellar.insetCm; decision is S11's, built at M3a with the retaining walls.

basementDoor(doc: Document, key: PlatKey, b: Building): {side (Basement.ring side index), at PointCm} or null; written basementDoor(b), called on the building's own document and arena key; reads Basement.ring and .access, from M6-U the crypt's vault (Basement.crypt with capped bays, derived), Entrance records, wings (ground(b), stair wings' rings and stair 0's approach, V02 stairChain), RetainingWalls with V01 stepProfile(wall) (BCR-43), V05 levelledGroundCm (BCR-V5-30), cells moduleCm, door.mainCm, cellar.insetCm, cellar.depthCm; draws nothing and reads no plan; in @plat/plots beside facadeBays, re-exported by @plat/buildings (BCR-V2-18 precedent); built at M3a (file f item 578), so plan step 3 (BCR-V3-32), V01 entrance reserve (V1-3.8.2 step 5), T28-3 and exports read one door without elaborating. null unless Basement.access is external.

basementDoor door sides: sides of Basement.ring at least two moduleCm long (a door's width, §2.6 step 3), each read at its door point = midpoint, except on a building with Basement.crypt and ground(b) (church entered from above by crypt stairs, or crypt beside a storeyed wing entered via O2's crypt join): there the point nearest the midpoint (ties toward first vertex) at which the door's span (two moduleCm centred, within the side) shares no length with the crypt's vault; a side with no such point is no door side. Vault = Basement.crypt.ring plus capped bays (the step-2 ring, never moved by rank trim/re-growth, so no event at another church moves this door), or the author's ring where edited; before M6-U (file f item 238) every door point is a midpoint.

basementDoor rules, first giving a side wins: 1 wall walk-out: door sides whose door point lies within 2 x cellar.insetCm of a RetainingWall's high side whose step there (stepProfile at the nearest chain point) >= cellar.depthCm/2: the one with the largest step, ties nearer wall then ring index, at = door point; where the test (read at the midpoint of a non-door side) holds only for non-door sides, result null while ground(b) exists (trapdoor fallback, reported), never a door on a side away from the wall; without ground(b) rule 2 follows. 2 tomb door where ground(b) absent (V02 BCR-V2-33's one condition): an outside stair down to a door at the basement floor in the face of a ground-standing wing on the main entrance's side, on the door side nearest that face, outside every stair wing's ring and stair 0's approach, at = that side's point nearest the main entrance moved until the door's width lies within it (reported tombDoor); a crypt inside a solid tier 0 (V2C-68) is entered by the same door at its own floor; the tomb door is the basement's root (T28-2 external clause). 3 fall walk-out: the door side whose outside ground is lowest (levelledGroundCm at cellar.insetCm + door.mainCm outward from the door point along the outward normal, on a RetainingWall's far side where the point lies across one), ties ring index. No door side at all -> null (trapdoor fallback, reported). The plan opens an Opening door of door.entranceCm on storey -1's wall along side centred at at, with the base's outside stair (step 3); whichever rule places it, the door is the basement's root (O2). Every input eager: a RetainingWall, terrain, levelling, wing, entrance or basement change (incl. crypt vault from M6-U) moves it and marks the plan stale via BCR-V3-28's digest or the basement's change (§2.8).

Access heads: every AccessPoint in BuildingInput.accesses (ground.host this building or its basement, whatever source: neighbourhood, basement, system, lifeline, edit, and V04's dig, opening, overlap, crypt, dossier; or cause; BCR-V3-19; V4 §2.2) gets exactly one head, in access-id order, before any cut.

Heads (0) decks (item 110 (d)): a building with onDeck(b) (exactly the buildings V02's deck gate BCR-V2-34 denies a cellar, a placed landmark at a mole's head or mid-mole included, J-V2.68; a bank quay excepted by DeckContext.surfaceCm null) hosts no head and no well; an access V04 hands one anyway is headed as a hatch on level 0, reported W_DECK_ACCESS; a well pin there stays V04's, unheaded (reported).

Heads (1) storey: stair, cellar_stair, ladder, hatch, shaft, door head on the building's lowest storey (deepest basement storey, else level 0 where ground(b) exists); with neither (solid stack without basement) an outside door in the face of a ground-standing wing, its descent the access's own stairwell (V04), reported W_STACK_ACCESS: head storey null, no room, no Opening, door = stackAccessDoor(b,a) (the one point V01's entrance reserve reads), drawn door.entranceCm wide at at; a well heads on level 0 where ground(b) exists, else stays V04's pin, unheaded (reported); a crypt join (cause crypt) heads on storey -1 in the crypt; any other kind (sinkhole, collapsed_shaft, ruin_entrance under a footprint) headed as a hatch (outside door form on a building with neither basement nor ground(b)), reported.

stackAccessDoor(b: Building, a: AccessPoint): {wing BaseWing.key, side, at PointCm, fallback? true} or null; null unless the building has no basement and ground(b) absent; reads only the wings (on, solid, role, rings), V02 stairChain (stair 0 and its approach strip as V2 §4.6 bounds it: none under stair form none), a.ground.at, cell moduleCm; draws nothing, reads no plan; in @plat/plots beside basementDoor(b), re-exported by @plat/buildings; built at M3a so V01's entrance reserve (M5) reads it before any plan. Terms: outline = edge of the area ground-standing wings (no on) cover together; door part = maximal stretch of a wing ring side on the outline at least two moduleCm long; admissible point = at least one moduleCm from each end of its part with span (one moduleCm either side) at least one moduleCm from stair 0's approach strip. Wing: among non-stair ground-standing wings holding an admissible point, the one whose ring lies nearest a.ground.at (0 if it holds the point; ties key); side: that wing's side whose admissible points lie nearest (ties side index); at: projection of a.ground.at onto the side moved the least distance to be admissible (ties toward first vertex); fallback: no admissible point on any non-stair ground wing -> midpoint of the outline side nearest a.ground.at among every ground-standing wing's sides incl. stair 0 (ties wing key, side index), fallback set, reported W_STACK_ACCESS note door fallback. distCm measured to at; a wing, stack or stair change moves the door; the access's change or re-derivation marks the plan stale.

Heads (2) form: stair and cellar_stair = bay of one flight (S1 at the access's drop where drop <= head storey height (cellar.depthCm, else level 0 storeyCm), else S1 at that height, trying straight, dogleg, winder, spiral in S4 order; rest of the descent is the access's own stairwell (V04), never cut into the plan); ladder = ladder bay; hatch = Opening trapdoor with point over a ladder bay; door = Opening door on the head storey's wall segment nearest the element at the nearest point; shaft = square of access.shaftCm with a ladder; well = disc of access.wellCm (parapet incl.) as a 16-gon. (3) Through-rings: a well's or shaft's ring is a fixed ring on every storey from its head down to the lowest basement storey, a face of role shaft (never allocated, furnished or entered but at its head).

Heads (4) air: an access of role air (V04 L1 air shaft through a building) rides the chimney stack nearest ground.at within access.snapCm (Chimney.air names it; stack levels extend down to the lowest storey); with no stack in reach, a hearthless stack from the lowest storey to the roof placed by H2 (b)-(d) (drawn on the roof as a stack §8.6), reported; on a building with neither basement nor ground(b) it takes (1)'s outside-door form (a vent in the foot), storey null. (5) Position: module candidates ranked by distance from ground.at (stair bay against a wall of its piece as S2; shaft, well, hatch anywhere in the piece keeping minEdge) excluding clearance squares, aprons, the core's bay, crypt columns and other heads; first within access.snapCm taken else nearest, reported in PlanReport.anchors with distCm; a null-storey head takes (1)'s door point, distCm to door.at; the head is the drawn position at the building band, the underground part keeps ground.at, the two scenes link by access id.

Heads (6) host room: first role in the AccessHostRow order for the reached element's system kind and the access's cause (row with cause wins) present on the head's storey; the ProgramRoom holding it takes anchor.access; none present -> A2 (10) added one; null-storey head has none. On a crypt-only basement (storey -1 is the crypt's and capped bays' pieces alone) a head whose reach is not a catacomb lies in the capped bays' undercroft where one exists else in the crypt, reported (access, tier 2, note crypt host). A crypt join (cause crypt, V04 U-ACCESS (c)) is the only catacomb head a crypt holds; any other catacomb head (burial ground's chapel stair, V4 §3.5.1 (9)) lies in a cellar, the chapel's nave or a store. A church-class building (crypt column always or basement) never hosts a catacomb access of source system: should V04 hand one the plan heads it in a store, reports W_CHURCH_CATACOMB_HEAD, and T-V3-23 (d) fails the fixture.

Heads (7) opening and state: the head's opening enters it from its host room (open for a stair or ladder bay, the hatch's trapdoor, the door itself), outside the host's maxDoors; a null-storey head has no Opening. The access's state as II.7.4 reads it (stored state, or while its element is closed (II.6) the derived reading: bricked while sealed; collapsed while partly caved in or collapsed) is drawn and exported: open as drawn; locked a closed locked door or hatch; bricked the opening drawn as wall with a bricking hatch, left out of every portal; collapsed the opening drawn as a trace with rubble stipple (§8.2 access row, as V01 V1-3.8.8 draws the surface symbol), left out of every portal; read at draw and export time, never stored on the head, so a closure change (II.6 conversions, V06 epochs) redraws the head's storey (its DisplayDelta) without re-cutting the plan.

Secret head: a head whose access's knownTo is secret gets, before the storey's cut, its own concealed room: a fixed ring of role back room, area = role min x ladder sizeFactor and at least the head's ring plus landingCm in front, against the head storey's wall nearest the element (head placed inside it); concealed, scope service; the rest of the storey keeps its scope and no concealed flag; joined by one concealed opening to the cellar, or to the concealed suite where one lies on that storey (O6); a local or public head stays in its host room; the same for a secret head on a ground storey (a hovel's hidden shaft).

Crypt derived with the basement, never by the plan, from V11's three-valued crypt column (BCR-V11-13): always (V11 cathedral, great_temple, and any building a dossier crypt record binds to, V4 §2.3a): basement by the no-refusal crypt ladder full, then half, then raised (V2 §3.14.5 (d), Basement.kind raised, BCR-V2-28; on a sky island V05's rim-slab vault V5 §3.10 (5), planned as full) in place of the class probability and the terrain gate's no-cellar rows; where the class's ordinary cellar draw also gives a basement the crypt lies inside it; otherwise, where the crypt is stair-entered or ground(b) absent, crypt-only (Basement.ring = the crypt's ring, floors 1, access core with the crypt stairs as cores so T28-3 holds; external by basementDoor(b) where ground(b) absent: tomb door or wall walk-out door; a great temple built as a solid stack, seed wing its tier 0, V2 §3.15.3); where ground(b) exists but the crypt would not be stair-entered, never crypt-only: the region whole (§2.6 inset of the ground wings, BCR-V2-33), crypt inside, floors 1, access the programme row's (external only for a walk-out), core or trapdoor in the part under the storeyed wing, an outside door off the vault, O2's crypt join enters the crypt (J-V3.127). On the raised rung V02 lifts every ground wing over that whole inset so its ground storey clears the basement by crypt.clearCm and its core reaches the basement beside the crypt; a solid tier 0 holding the crypt keeps its height (J-V3.128). An author's crypt ring on a building without a basement makes a basement by the same ladder (crypt-only, or whole inset where not stair-entered; V3C-75). basement: base decision unchanged; full, half or walkout basement holds a crypt, crawl space none (V11's religious cellar rows are then the crypt's chance). never: no crypt.

Crypt ring in three steps on the lattice in area2: (1) seed: the part of the basement's region (Basement.ring; for crypt-only, the ring the basement would take, §2.6 inset of ground wings) under cryptSeedWings(b) (V2 §3.14.5 (c), @plat/plots), else the third of the region farthest from the main entrance along the footprint's OBB long axis; (2) growth to V11 cryptM2 target T for the class at the occupants' band (four-column cell): seed > T trimmed from its end nearer the main entrance by a cut perpendicular to the long axis at the module position giving T (slice's search); short -> grows toward the main entrance by the slab between its entrance-side edge and a parallel line whose module position gives T (bisection), never beyond the region; on half and raised rungs never beyond the ground wings its seed lies under (or the solid tier 0 holding it) so a half-sunk or raised crypt stays under its raised choir; a region smaller than T becomes the crypt whole (reported); a crypt so bounded below T reported short; an author's ring keeps no bound (V02 raises or lifts wings over it).

Crypt rank (3): principal crypt = the cathedral building's (several: largest ring, ties address); no cathedral: the always building with largest ring (ties address); no always building: none. Every other crypt's ring capped at crypt.rankShare (V11 row, default 0.8) x principal's area: its step-2 ring trimmed from its entrance end by step 2's cut where it exceeds the cap. The trim shortens Basement.crypt.ring only, never Basement.ring; capped bays (step-2 ring less trimmed ring, inside Basement.ring; derived) planned as one undercroft room under the crypt's column grid, vaults kept and drawn. Rank recomputed, never only a trim: each run caps every ranked crypt afresh from its step-2 ring (deterministic, no draw), so when the principal's area falls, moves, or the trimmed building becomes principal, its ring re-grows within Basement.ring up to its step-2 ring and the capped bays regain the crypt role. The rank runs as a closing pass of S11 over every building with a crypt (BCR-V3-20), and again inside the causing event whenever the principal crypt, its building or area changes (others' plans marked stale or re-cut, §7.3); V11's compile bar keeps every always class's smallest cryptM2 above every basement class's largest, so at generation the trim is a backstop save where the half or raised bound leaves the principal short; across epochs V06 re-runs the rank inside each op that moves the see (V6 §3.18.3 (2)-(3)).

Stair-entered crypt: where ground(b) exists and the ring of a storeyed ground-standing wing (BaseWing.on absent, s0(w) = 0) shares area with its vault (step-2 ring holding its capped bays, or the author's ring where edited); derived, never stored, no rank event moves it; entered by its crypt stairs (3.7.6); any other (ground(b) absent, or no storeyed wing over its vault) is entered from the basement by basementDoor(b) or O2's one crypt join; the basement function reads it before fixing the basement's extent, on the step-2 ring of the region a crypt-only basement would take; built with the crypt derivation at M6-U (file f item 238; §8 P2).

An author's ring (setAttr(basement) on basement/crypt/ring, edited true) is kept and never trimmed; a rank or always-rule it breaks is announced and reported; a dossier crypt record makes its building always. No plan derivation writes Basement.crypt: the plan reads it (T-V3-23 (f)), so V04 crypt join (V4 §3.5.7 (c)), the rank, V10's why and V01 T-V1-47 read it at generation without elaborating any building. A church-class building without a crypt furnishes its chancel with flush ledger slabs (3.8): no opening, no join, no floor-vault crypt.

Crypt's plan: the crypt ring is a fixed seed piece of storey -1 cut out of Basement.ring before A5 allocates the rest, holding one crypt room (nave pattern); capped bays are a second fixed seed piece holding one undercroft room (nave pattern), joined to the crypt by one arch of door.archCm on their shared wall and, only where the crypt is not stair-entered, to the rest of storey -1 as any room is (O2). Columns: in the step-2 ring's OBB frame (an edited ring's own), a grid of pitch crypt.bayCm centred on that OBB (does not move when rank trims or re-grows); a square of crypt.columnCm at every grid node at least crypt.bayCm/2 inside the crypt's ring or the capped bays' ring and outside every stair bay and head; each a fixed column ring that the cut avoids and F3 furnishes around. The crypt's boundary moves only with Basement.crypt.ring (a moveWall on it bends to setAttr(basement), 4.2); its walls above ground in the raised form take W2 light windows.

Crypt stairs and choir flights: the crypt's nave-side edge = its ring edge crossing the footprint's long axis nearer the main entrance; on storey 0 the same line is the nave/chancel line. Where they start: crypt stairs laid only to a stair-entered crypt; they and choir flights laid only from a nave piece on level 0; where ground(b) holds no nave, from the largest level-0 room whose piece stands over part of the crypt's ring along its nave-side edge, else from the largest level-0 room over part of its vault, the flight's bay inside that part, landing in the crypt else in the capped bays' undercroft; where not stair-entered (ground(b) absent or no storeyed wing over the vault) the entry is from the basement (basementDoor(b) directly or O2's crypt join), reported cryptStair noted tomb door or crypt join; no stair descends through a solid wing.

(a) Crypt stairs full and half forms: straight S1 flights at delta = floorCm(nave's wing, 0) - crypt floor, width stair.flightCm.institution, each a StairCore of levels [-1,0] whose bay lies inside the crypt's ring against its nave-side edge, long axis along the church axis descending away from the nave; two flank the axis at +/-(minRoomWidthCm/2 + f/2) where the edge holds two flights and minRoomWidthCm between, else one on the side of the lower lattice index; on storey 0 the bay is a fixed ring in the piece above (chancel's west end where the crypt lies under the chancel alone), joined like a core's bay with the nave preferred (one open opening onto the nave or the first-reached room above); foot opens into the crypt; a bay that does not fit takes dogleg, winder, spiral, then one ladder bay (tier 2, reported cryptStair). (b) Raised form crypt entry: one StairCore [-1,0] centred on the axis at the nave-side edge, S1 straight at delta = abs(nave floor - crypt floor) (0 allowed: level bay of landingCm depth), width institution; on storey 0 under the lifted choir at the nave's floor joined to the nave by an arch; foot opens into the crypt.

(c) Choir flights: wherever a chancel piece's floorCm exceeds the adjacent nave piece's by more than datum.maxSteps x riserCm (V02 lift of crypt.clearCm or any other difference), two straight S1 flights at that difference, width institution, stand in the nave piece against the nave/chancel line rising toward the chancel, flanking the crypt entry at +/-(its width/2 + jambCm + f/2) in the raised form, else flanking the axis as (a); only one fits -> one on the lower lattice index side; none fits -> one flight against the nave's side wall at the line (tier 2), else tier 6 (flagged); each is a stair room with an open opening onto the nave at its foot and the chancel at its head (the O2 edge replacing O1 (c)'s refused door, so T28-2 holds). Where the crypt is stair-entered the crypt stairs are its entry and the vault is closed; where ground(b) exists the basement's outside door never opens into the vault; a crypt joined to a catacomb holds that access's head and nothing else links it underground.

Crawl space (kind crawl) is no storey: level 0 carries an Opening trapdoor with point in the room over the building's lowest footprint sample, nothing below is cut; where ground(b) is absent the hatch is an outside one at basementDoor(b) (access external by V02 BCR-V2-33), else where that is null in the face of the ground-standing wing nearest the main entrance, reported.

F1 count: per room n = density x area m2 (role density interpolated x resolved row furnish.density multiplier), fraction drawn once on plan.furnish; 0 in circulation, passage and structural rooms and in a vacant or ruined plan. F2 free floor: room ring less every opening's clearance square, every stair bay with its first-step apron (landingCm), every stack's apron, every head's ring with landingCm in front of a stair or ladder head, every Opening.steps flight footprint, every column, and a walkwayCm band along the tree path through the room (door to door).

F3 place: glyphs = role list filtered by row band; ledger only in a chancel of a church-class building without a crypt; brazier only by 3.12; tomb in a crypt stands free between columns; glyphs drawn by row weights on plan.furnish, largest first, capped at perRoomMax; first round(n x wallBias) items to wall slots (against items at slots scanned along walls from the corner farthest from the entry door, counter-clockwise, on the module; corner items in corners first); rest by placement: row items (pews) in rows across the long axis from the altar end with clearCm aisles; free items at the room's spine summit (base §3.8 spine reader) then along the spine; rotCdeg: against/corner/row = wall direction, free = OBB long axis, integer centidegrees via dmath (§6.5 (2)); fit test uses the rotated rectangle plus clearCm in front inside F2; tall items keep off window bays; an altar stands first, centred against the wall farthest from the entry door; none fitting -> skipped (counted); nothing over an opening's clearance square, stair bay, head or apron (§2.6 step 6). F4 ids in placement order (2.2); Room.nextFurniture = count.

Failure table (F-PLAN tiers): household does not fit at its form (A5 (a)) -> 0 next poorer form, never omitted, at room the no-abort ladder; soft room does not fit (A5 (d)) -> 0 dropped, 5 later if a cut leaves it below min; hard non-unit room (A5 (b)) -> ladder step (ii), 6 omitted only after every unit reached its form or room; no stair candidate (S4) -> 2 next kind, 6 upper storeys unreached; no stack candidate (H2) -> 2 next preference, (e) hood, 6 hearth omitted room kept; anchor or head ring refused by arena -> 2 next candidate same attempt (no stream read); head beyond access.snapCm -> 2 nearest, distance reported; no shared-access strip -> 2 core re-scored, then lobby with O5 strips; cut part below minWidthCm everywhere (slice) -> 2 slide to neighbour's minimum, 3 re-run pattern on next plan.layout attempt (<= 3), 4 bisect on the wing's axes; room unreached or unit without own door (O2, O5) -> 2 O5 strip, 5 soft room absorbed into circulation, 1 flagged; floors too far apart (O1 (c)) -> wings unjoined (S5), a stair hall flight or choir flights, joinsRefused; crypt stair or choir flight not fitting -> 2 next kind, one flight, side wall, 6 flagged; hard room missing after the cut (P5) -> 5 generic room where free, 6 omitted flagged; seed, passage or composer ring refused (tileRings, transientArena) -> the rung aborts with its stream key (composer's or caller's bug, §2.6 contract), building draws its wings, flagged; work limit on a storey -> 3 next attempt, 4 bisect, then 6 for remaining soft rooms; chain core fits no whole chain -> 2 longest prefix; landing door beyond snapCm -> 2 side midpoint; stacked wing joined by nothing -> 1 W_TIER_UNREACHED; building with no storeyed wing -> none, solidMonument; no nave over a stair-entered crypt -> largest level-0 room over part of the vault; crypt not stair-entered -> basementDoor(b) or O2 crypt join, where the basement is unreached base fallback tier 1; external basement with basementDoor null -> 2 base trapdoor fallback reported core noted no basement door, where its bay does not fit (always so without ground(b)) basement unreachable tier 1; hosted access on a solid stack without basement -> 2 outside door at stackAccessDoor, W_STACK_ACCESS (door fallback); access or well on a deck -> 2 hatch on level 0, W_DECK_ACCESS, well unheaded; secondary entrance meets no floor -> not derived, W_ENTRANCE_NO_STOREY; main entrance far above ground -> stoop uncapped; stepped temple soft rooms with no storey below the shrine -> 0 dropped, shrineOneRoom; grade face holding an entrance marked tunnel -> drawn and exported as yard, W_GRADE_FACE_TUNNEL.

No-abort fit ladder, run in order until every household has a unit, each step in PlanReport.fit: (i) dropSoft every soft room dropped; (ii) omitHard hard non-unit rooms omitted, last in list order first (tier 6); (iii) reduceCirculation to the core's landings and O5's unit door strips; (iv) stairDown the stair kind stepped down S4's order to the smallest bay that fits; (v) minimalRooms room units cut at the capacity's own minRoomCm2 with minWidthCm relaxed to minRoomWidthCm. BCR-V3-12 subtracts from §2.6's capacity, on every storey above the lowest a core serves, a ladder bay and a landing, so step (v) always fits a shell at capacity; a table edit that would break that re-homes the excess before any plan runs; no plan aborts for want of room (T-V3-17); nothing outside the building is touched; every tier lands in PlanReport.

Streams (§6.1 key layout: lineage and rung counters, then creation index): plan.program draws A2's fractional counts only, index (origin, rule, household ordinal or 0); plan.layout draws the pattern per storey class, index (storey class), and each tie between equal-score cut positions, index (storey level, attempt, cut ordinal in the storey's cut order), attempt counter per storey level cap 3; plan.roles draws P7's permutation per exchange class, index (storey level, class index in piece order); plan.furnish draws F1's fraction and F3's glyph choices, index (room address), draws in placement order within the room.

Every other choice is a total order (score, lowest-leftmost lattice point, list order, wing key); all arithmetic integer on area2 and lattice points except slice's ratio (ratio(), §3.2 (8)), the spiral's and well's 16-gons and rotCdeg (dmath, §6.5 (2)); a plan is a function of §2.6 step 1's inputs and the rung counters; a whole derivation and the same state reached by any local re-derivation of 4.2 on an unstored plan are byte-identical (T-V3-20); item 110's rules add no draw (level reading, storey heights, chain cores, S6 joins, terraces, exposure, entrance storeys, tomb door, grade faces are total orders) so plan.layout or plan.roles re-rolls keep them.

Re-cuts (§2.6 canonical chain; stored plan re-cut §7.3) run 3.1 with prior: seeds and anchors (core bay, stacks, entrances, passage and composer rooms, crypt ring, columns and stairs, choir flights, heads) unchanged by construction unless their own inputs changed (a head whose access changed is re-placed); A5 allocates the new programme and A6's strip is cut first. Kept-room test before any other cut: a prior room is kept (passed as fixed, §3.4) when its seed piece is unchanged, its ring meets no new A6 strip, its area lies in [min,max] of a still-unassigned role of the new programme on its storey (best fit first: target nearest, ties list order); a unit room only where the same household is still housed; the rest cut as new, rooms minted from the level's highest id + 1. On a stack, a wing standing on another is compared by wing-relative storey s - s0(w), so a tiers edit adding a storey below shifts no room above out of its match (kept rooms keep ids, openings, windows, furniture, locks, edited attributes); a room whose wing is removed or whose wing-relative storey no longer exists is orphaned and reported (§7.4 plan-event row) and listed in the edit's dry run. Kept openings: every kept opening re-checked against O2's forbidden set under the new units and concealment and new maxDoors; failing ones removed (reported); O2 re-derives the tree with the passing ones as forced edges. The report counts kept rooms (T-V3-9's mutation-survival figure); each chain step is one derivation keyed by the step's target (§6.1).

Buildings below ground (ContextVector.arena underground: sewer-front dwelling II.7.3, undercity building II.7.5, cavern or ruin dwelling once an access exists, item 109 (e), (j)(4)) take 3.1-3.11 with differences: (1) no basement (3.7.1, 3.7.4-3.7.7 do not run; a head, none by V04's rules, would be on level 0); (2) no windows and no dormers except on a grade face; lit stays the role's, light a lamp by V04's underground light rows (V4 §3.9, §4.7's light table in the underground arena); (3) hearths: first a face flue on a grade face, else a flue on the room's wall nearest the frontage carried to the nearest air access within hearth.flueReachM (a Chimney whose column is the flue's wall point, levels its own storey, air that access, drawn as a flue mark, never a roof stack); no air access in reach -> brazier (Room.hearth absent, one brazier glyph by F3, reported flue); no stack ever rises through the ground; (4) frontage door onto its tunnel run, gallery or undercity walkway, Entrance.faces tunnel written by V04's derivation, except on a grade face; (5) walls keep §2.6 kinds, the draw styles exterior walls by host (tunnel masonry, cavern rock, item 109 (g) ruin masonry) from the building's part, no new wall kind; (6) a ruin chamber's columns (V4 §3.5.0a ruinColumns(chamberId), C4-64 (5)) are fixed column rings; (7) storeys are the building's Heights as V04 derives them under its host's headroom; (8) the plan's draw and per-storey VTT scene sit at the underground band's depth (§11.1).
