Grade faces (item 110 (b); II.7.5, II.7.6): a side of the host chamber (V04 chamber whose ring holds the footprint on its part) that V04 marks open to ground part 0 is a grade face: an arch vault's open face between two piers (V04 archVault chambers, C4-110-1), a bridge approach's or street vault's open arch; the wall on it is exterior at grade: W1-W3 run (windows in the arch's infill, V02 facadeBays on that side, outsideCm the ground under the span); the frontage entrance faces the way or ground under the span (street, lane, alley, or yard; never tunnel - one written tunnel is drawn and exported as yard, reported W_GRADE_FACE_TUNNEL); a hearth's flue on it is a Chimney whose levels are its own storey, drawn as a flue mark on the face, never a roof stack. Pre-decided fallback until V04 records its marks: an archVault chamber's grade faces are the two sides of its rectangle parallel to its raised way's axis (arch mouths); any other chamber has none. Storeys stay under the vault's soffit by V02's clamp (V2C-67 (2)). Removing a raised way (a user's removal holds through regeneration, item 110 (b)) takes its vault chambers and their buildings by the base's least-disruption fates; the dry run lists each such building and, where its plan is stored, 'its edited floor plan is lost' with named rooms and placed items counted; undo restores the building with its stored plan byte for byte.

A ruin's stepped monument is V04's chamber record (Chamber.monument, C4-110-8), laid by V02's layTiers and decayed there, not a building, no plan; an underground building never overlaps it (V04 treats its tiers as obstacles); V3C-65 (4)'s 'these rules unchanged below ground' binds only a building below ground standing on another wing, which the level reading covers.

Every plan edit is an event of §7.1 emitted by an existing tool (§7.1 authoring toolkit); V03 adds parameters and attribute paths, never a thirteenth tool (§13.2 elegance bars). Tool map: T9 shape -> setRoomRole, moveWall, splitRoom, mergeRooms, setOpening (hinge, swing; BCR-V3-24), setWindow (kind; BCR-V3-24), moveStairCore (kind; BCR-V3-3), setHearth (BCR-V3-3), setRoomUnit, instance on a room's furniture (BCR-V3-4), setEntrance, setAttr on basement (incl. basement/crypt/ring), declaredRooms (BCR-V3-15), plan/rooms/<id>/lit, plan/pattern/<level>; T11 name -> setAttr plan/rooms/<id>/name; T10 hold -> lock on plan/rooms/<id>, regenerate with rung (plan, plan.layout, plan.roles, plan.furnish); T6 place -> convert relet (household count within capacity; BCR-V3-16); T2 ground -> addUndergroundAccess stays the underground tools' (item 66), effect a head re-anchored; T9 (V02 tier controls), T3 wall retaining, T4 road raised -> no plan event (owners'), effect via 4.2 re-match, stale mark or fate line. A clerk emits the same events via the tool API (§11.2), dry-run first, proposedBy clerk.

Edit semantics: plan events, setRoomRole and regenerate with rung are §7.1's; dry runs check §13.2's plan bars on the overlay; per item 101 R2 an edit that cannot be done exactly is bent to the nearest lawful form and the bend named in one line; refused only against a dossier fact or a lock; local re-derivations draw at 3.10's indices so a plan reached through them equals the whole derivation's (T-V3-20).

setRoomRole: roles only; re-derives the room's door kinds and widths (O3; a changed width re-centred on the same midpoint), windows (W1-W3 on its walls), furniture (F1-F4 in that room, ids re-issued from nextFurniture), lit and label; no ring or opening position moves; a role whose storey rule or area range the room breaks is kept as declared and the report notes the rule. moveWall, splitRoom, mergeRooms: storey rooms either side re-take O1-O6 for touched walls, W1-W3 for touched exterior walls, F1-F4 for touched rooms; other rooms' parts keep ids; a wall moved past minWidthCm or into a fixed ring stops at the nearest lawful module position (bend named); a moveWall on the crypt's boundary is carried out as setAttr(basement) on basement/crypt/ring (announced).

setOpening (hinge, swing) and setWindow (kind): the named part only; a moved door re-takes O3's hinge and swing unless given; F2's clearance re-checked, furniture in a clearance square moves by F3 within its room (listed in fates); a door onto a forbidden edge bends to the nearest wall of the same room whose other side is allowed; a door on an exterior wall is lawful where the outside is ground within datum tolerance or a walkable terrace (a door set onto a roof terrace makes it walkable) else bent to the nearest such wall of the same room ('no door into earth: moved to the street side'); a window set below its outside ground bends up to the lowest bay whose sill clears it, else to the nearest wall with one, named.

moveStairCore (kind): the bay on every storey it serves, each re-partitioned around it (3.11); a kind whose bay does not fit takes the nearest kind in S4's order that fits; a position fitting no kind takes S2's nearest candidate; bends named. setHearth {building, storey, room, op add/move/remove, wall?, at?}: stack re-placed by H2-H3 constrained to the named wall and position, rising as H2 states; a wall that cannot take a stack bends to the nearest wall of the room that can in H2's order; every crossed storey re-cut (3.11); removing the last hearth on a stack removes the Chimney and its roof stack (§8.6).

instance on a room: entity = room id, ordinal = furniture ordinal (decimal string): add (glyph at a point, ordinal Room.nextFurniture), move (to a point snapped to 10 cm), remove, restyle (style.glyph, rotCdeg, wCm, dCm; sizes clamped into the row's range, named); an add or move onto a spot F2 forbids snaps to the nearest free slot of F3's scan in the room (named); no free slot -> bends to the nearest room of the building with one (same storey by centroid distance, else nearest storey ties lower, ties room id) placed by F3's scan and named ('no room for a bed in the pantry: placed in the chamber'); a moved item bending into another room takes that room's nextFurniture (new id; fates list the old); no room with a free slot -> kept where put and reported as crowding; nothing refused; item marked edited.

setAttr declaredRooms: declared rooms become A2 (7)'s hard rooms; unstored plan marked stale, stored re-cut inside the event; a room not fitting its declared storey bends to the nearest storey holding it (ties lower); fitting nowhere first displaces soft rooms then other hard non-unit rooms (ladder (i)-(ii)), named; refused only where every household's unit leaves no room, naming that cause (households are the dossier's population, item 20 (h)). setAttr plan/rooms/<id>/name (T11): label shows it, role unchanged, stores the plan; .../lit: light on/off (edited attribute §7.2; Dwellings' per-room toggle), stores the plan; plan/pattern/<level>: re-cuts that storey by 3.11 with the named LayoutPattern for every piece holding its requirement (others by 3.5's rule, named), stores the plan.

setAttr(basement) incl. basement/crypt/ring: basement storeys re-cut (3.11); crypt re-derived by 3.7.4 unless its ring is the path set; hosted accesses re-read after the underground rules re-run for this building (II.7.3 gate and draw, V04 per-building crypt-join and dig-from-above draws V4 §3.5.7 (c),(d), keyed per building so the same uniform decides at the new floor, owned by V04), heads re-anchored; dry run names one line each every access gained, lost or re-hosted and, where a lost one was a void's last access, the dwellings item 109 (j)(4) would empty (V04 excavation reading V4 §3.5.7 (g): 'removing this cellar seals the only way into the ruin: 4 households leave'); an edit removing an always building's crypt or shrinking the principal below another is kept as the author's and announced, reported in PlanReport.anchors (crypt, note); a change of the principal's area re-runs the rank for every other crypt, named in the preview.

setAttr(basement) on basement/crypt/ring of a building without a basement (V3C-75): makes a crypt-only basement by the no-refusal crypt ladder (full, half, raised), or the ground wings' whole inset where the ring would not be stair-entered, as a dossier crypt record does: building always for that derivation, Basement.crypt.edited set, ring = given ring clipped to 3.7.4 step 1's region and snapped to the lattice; access = crypt stairs where stair-entered, the programme row's with O2's crypt join where ground(b) exists but not stair-entered, or the tomb door where ground(b) absent; on a never class kept and announced ('by the rules this building has no crypt; kept as yours'); the terrain gate never refuses (raised always lawful); V09's drawChamber bend inside a church-class footprint emits exactly this event.

Deck bend: on a deck building (onDeck(b)) every basement form fails at once and the request bends (item 101 R2) to the same request on the nearest building on the ground of its plot group, else of its block, else the nearest building on the ground, named bend.deck.basement (BCR-V2-34 as file f item 305 words it; V02 registers the id for V09 and V10): 'A deck over water holds no cellar: the cellar goes to <building> on the quay.'; dry run previews that building's basement and consequences; a deck is a map fact, neither dossier fact nor lock, so nothing is refused.

Owners' edits reaching the plan: V02's tiers op and stepped mutations re-cut a stored plan by 3.11's wing-relative re-match (unstored goes stale); the op's dry run lists from V03 every named, locked or furnished room and every edited opening of a removed tier (or removed wing-relative storey) as 'orphaned: <room name or role>, tier k'; each undo restores byte for byte. A RetainingWall drawn, moved or removed (T3 wall retaining, T2 ground): each building whose outside digest it moves (BCR-V3-28) has its unstored plan marked stale and stored plan re-cut inside the event (W2 gates re-run, walk-out re-decided), both listed in fates; undo restores byte for byte. Removing a raised way: among its fates, each building in its vaults and, for a stored plan, 'its edited floor plan is lost' with named rooms and placed items counted; V09 and V10 read the fates; undo restores them.

The first plan edit on a building stores its composition with its plan (§2.6) under J-P48 (1) in the same batch; setAttr declaredRooms and setAttr(basement) are building attributes and store the plan only when already stored; the three owners' edits store nothing here.

Locality: every plan edit's effective scope is its building (§7.3 item 1), plus for the storing edit the faces J-P48 (1)'s split vertices touch; nothing outside re-derived (T28-7), except setAttr(basement)'s underground consequences (V04's, named in the preview) and the rank of the other crypts when the principal's area changes (their plans stale, stored re-cut in the same event); three outside edits reach a plan by their owners' scope: a RetainingWall's (outside digest, BCR-V3-28), a raised way's removal (vault fates), a deck's ruin or removal (item 110 (d): buildings fall with it, 5.1).

Stored plans: an edited room, locked room (plan/rooms/<id>), edited opening, window, hearth, stair core, furniture item or crypt ring is a fixed input of every later re-cut (§7.2); a stored plan whose inputs change is re-cut inside the changing event around them (§7.3 table) by 3.11 with edited parts as fixed rings and openings; an edited part no longer fitting the new shell is orphaned and reported (§7.4 plan-event row).

Carries: BCR-V3-2 adds each Storey.furniture[].at to the points carryWings carries with a stored plan (§2.6 CarriedShapes.composition, J-P48); after each carry each item is checked (footprint inside its room's carried ring, off every clearance square, stair bay, head and apron); failing -> re-snapped by F3's slot scan within its room with no draw (a fate, reported), else orphaned (§7.3 item 4); an opening whose at + widthCm/2 + jambCm exceeds its carried wall's length is clamped to the wall's end and reported.

New random on an edited plan (regenerate with rung): plan.furnish re-places every non-edited item by F1-F4 on the advanced counter; plan.roles runs P7 over exchange classes excluding edited and locked rooms; plan.layout re-cuts the stored plan by 3.11 around edited and locked parts with the advanced counter; plan = all three; each compared by §5.1 (6) on the stored subtree and reported when nothing changed (never a silent no-op).

Undo: each event's undo record is the former storeys it touched (§7.4): setHearth every storey its stack crosses; moveStairCore every storey the core serves; setAttr(basement) basement, crypt, hosted accesses and plan in one step; setAttr declaredRooms former value and plan. Lifecycle rows: setHearth, instance on a room and plan attribute paths use §7.4's plan-event row (BCR-V3-4, BCR-V3-16 add them by name); declaredRooms and basement use §7.4's setAttr row with the consequences above.

Not an edit: clicking a building, switching storeys, opening the plan panel, turning room numbers on (roomNumbers view key) and a clerk's plan or why query log nothing (§4.1, item 28 (c), §2.9 view state); a room's light is the edited attribute of 4.2; placeLight (§7.1, item 68) adds lights of its own and never changes a room's lit.

Plan states (§2.8) read on the building: absent (wings draw, panel offers Show plan); current (plan draws); stale (cached plan draws under §8.5's marker, panel says what changed: the input group whose digest moved - households, band, use, wings, an access, the crypt, the Works stage or a table - and the next building click, double-click or view re-derives it from its canonical prior §4.1); edited (stored plan draws, a pencil mark beside the marker slot).

Click and double-click (§14 input scheme): from the neighbourhood band down, a click selects the building, opens the plan panel and under elaborate 'click' derives wings, then rooms (V02 §3.8), then plan into the cache, each where absent or stale, without moving the view; at the city and district bands a click on a building is the district's click (V01 V1-3.8.1: close-up and its buildings' wings rung), also selecting the building and opening its panel without deriving rooms or plan (panel offers Show plan); a double-click or Show plan at any band derives wings, rooms, plan and zooms to the building band at the frame stop (coarsest stop at which the building's longest side fills view.frameShare 0.6 of the view, clamped to view.frameStops [1:125, 1:350]) and sets storey to the main entrance's storey (solid stack: the root landing door's; no storeyed wing: -1 where it has a basement); the plan arrives from the derivation pool as a DisplayDelta (§8.6), wings draw with a small progress tick meanwhile (no spinner); a stale building with a long re-cut chain derives its steps in the pool during idle frames (§6 chain row).

Storey switcher: vertical radio group beside the building, accessible name Storey, one option per storeyed level (-k..n) and per walkable roof level, named 'Storey n of m - cellar / ground / first ...' ('ground' only for level 0 where ground(b) exists), on a stack by wing role and ordinal ('Tier 2, storey 1', 'Shrine', 'Roof terrace'); a building with no storeyed wing lists only its basement storeys, with no basement has no switcher; the current is checked; the map region's live description gains 'storey n of m'; keymap.json rows plan.storeyUp (PageUp), plan.storeyDown (PageDown), editable, versioned (§14); view key storey (§2.9) holds it per viewer.

Plan panel (context panel building tab, accessible name Floor plan): rooms by storey with name or role, number (roomNumbers on), unit (household name for an admitted viewer) and area m2; what the plan owed (PlanReport.owed delivered in plain words) and units with forms; the ways down per storey (null-storey head under 'at the foot'): kind, state, what it reaches (element's system and via V04's connection graph systems beyond, item 109 (j)(3b)), cause in plain words, withheld for a key its knownTo does not admit; the crypt line; item 110 lines (solidMonument, W_TIER_UNREACHED, deck no cellar/no well, fell with the bridge/pier/mole/quay, exposure gate, walk-out, grade face); room numbers: per-viewer view key roomNumbers 'off'/'storey'/'building' in reading order (storey then room index) with a key table; every edit tool of 4.1 acts from the panel or canvas.

elaborate 'view' derives (wings, rooms, plan as a click does) and draws plans only at stops of view.planStop (1:350) or finer, and for at most view.planCap (64) buildings per view, centre-out, within §6's per-frame budget; the rest draw their wings.

Clerk queries: {kind 'plan', building, storey?} returns the plan's storeys as §11.1's JSON plan block, derived first (wings, rooms, plan each where absent or stale, as a click; the pool, no event, cache only); {kind 'planReport', building} returns PlanReport (a stored plan's recomputed); both filter by the caller's knowledge key (§9.2) by 5.4's merge (concealed room, door, head or furniture withheld, room merged into its public neighbour, areas re-summed, never a void); a clerk changes a plan only through 4.1's events via preview then edit.

Why provider for kind room (BCR-V10-3 interface): resolves a room: address through its building's plan (stored, else cache, else a derivation into the cache as the plan query; BCR-V3-22 lets V10's registry resolve plan addresses by prefix); answer facts = role, name, scope, household, area, storey, tier, accesses {id, kind, reaches, cause}[], elevationCm, room tier (wing role and ordinal); cause = ProgramRoom origin and rule (class, use, specialisation, half or slot row; ladder row and band; declared; crypt from V11 column and basement form; edit), pattern and cutting step, each head's cause, and for each door and missing window item 110's causes: landingDoor, terraceDoor, terraceExit, seatingExit, walkOut (basementDoor rule: retaining wall id and step, or the fall; on a church door point moved off the vault), tombDoor, gradeFace, deckNoCellar, stoop, exposure, stackCarried; rest = PlanReport.owed row and the unit's asked and built form. Building path plan ('why these units?', 'why is there no kitchen?', 'why no crypt?', 'why are there no rooms?', 'why can't I reach the top tier?') answers from the ladder row, Building.households, programmeSource, owed rows, Basement.crypt's derivation (column value, ladder form, rank trim) and PlanReport.warnings; both knowledge-filtered by V10's oracle rules and 5.4.

Stops: the pyramid gains eight stops past 1:500 at the same 2^(1/4) step to about 1:125, drawn only at the building band and only over buildings whose plan draws; the building band's threshold is the stop nearest 1:700 (entered there, left one stop coarser, §8.5 hysteresis); at 1:125 one CSS px is about 3.3 cm (80 cm door about 24 px; a 5 px label fits a 1.5 m room).

Detail ladder inside the building band by PlanGeometryRow.view stops: threshold to coarser than 1:350 walls by kind, openings as gaps, heads as solid symbols, room labels and lights only (no plan draws there under elaborate view); from leavesStop (1:350) door leaves and swings, windows, hearths, stair and flight outlines, wall shade, porch; from treadsStop (1:250) treads, furniture, slits, crypt columns, ledger slabs; the double-click frame stop never coarser than 1:350.

Marks and order (one DisplayDelta per building and storey, bottom to top): other storeys' wing outlines faded (§8.5); porch outline under the plan (V02 Porch and kind, halfRound half-disc); storey floor (ground in ink, lit roof tone in lit, §8.2); roof terraces (walkable T(x) as floor in the roof tone with parapet double line and doors; roof T(x) hatched as roof, never furnished); exterior flights of stairChain landing on the storey (treads by V02 stairTreads(w), n-1 lines at goingCm, arrow up, outside the walls; on a solid stack only as far as the solid wing it climbs); terrace exit stair house; stoop treads; wall shade paint program planWallShade (soft band of floor shade inside every wall, broken at openings, fading inward over 40 cm; our own); furniture (FurnitureRow shapes at ink alpha 0.5, fills in the furniture role in lit), ledger slabs flush outlines; stair flights (treads hairlines at goingCm, landing, arrow from lower storey's first step up; Plain words: the underground is built from rules, same seed, after the streets and houses exist; hidden until switched on; ground fades to a pale ghost and the underground appears as a dungeon-style map (rock dark and hatched, voids pale) one depth level at a time. Sewers first (sometimes in a town, always in a city), medieval practice: covered streams as main drains, big sewers under principal streets, always downhill to an outlet above the river or shore below harbour and mills, else a cess field outside the walls; size by drained area; most houses empty to the street or a pit, only wealthier houses and water trades connected; a grille where a sewer passes under the wall; realistic: few walkable; fantasy: large, vaulted, looped.

Plain words: people live along walkable sewers in rooms cut into both tunnel walls, one or two rooms deep, no alleys, never under a house, wall, river or wet ground (the town's poorest and those hiding). Catacombs grow only under cemeteries (churchyards, burial grounds, great cemeteries outside the gates), sized by their dead: at most one in a town, a few in a city by its number of churches, the largest under the cemetery burying most; a church keeps its own crypt (cathedral always, the largest); a crypt joins a catacomb only where one grows beneath. Caves follow water in limestone or old lava (more in mountains and where people mine; fissures in ordinary hill rock; a mine may break into a cave); old quarries sized by the stone the town was built from (a great city may make a quarry an ossuary); vaults carry streets over slopes and bridges onto banks; cisterns under the oldest precincts; a buried town where fire or flood raised the ground.

Plain words: under the arches of a viaduct, raised road or aqueduct some arches are walled in as vaults (store, stable, workshop back room), arches over a street, stream or steep ground stay open; any arch can be opened or closed; removing the raised way removes its vaults; a great cistern under the conduit house at the aqueduct's end, other cisterns only where neither river nor aqueduct fountains are near; sewers drop down a shaft at retaining walls; piers and wall footings fill a cave or ruin they meet. Older-than-the-town ruins (dossier or site reason: ancient ruins, magical node, history of magic) on their own plan, straight-walled and columned, decayed (halls survive, houses rubble), stepped monuments with fallen upper tiers and top cut where the ground presses.

Plain words: caves and ruins can lie under a hamlet as under a city; most start sealed; a house may dig down, a sinkhole or cave mouth may open it, a sewer or catacomb may cut through it (village rarely reaches it, city usually has, deepest chambers stay hidden under a metropolis); settled only once a way in exists (squatters or a cult; the undercity in a large place); a GM can show sealed voids. The undercity (at most one to three neighbourhoods) settles the largest reachable void, a ruin first, with market square, walkways, tavern, fence, guild seat, lifelines for air, water, food; each neighbourhood the shadow of a district above; trades within reach of their markets via the ways up, guild seat away from the garrison. Parts meet by typed openings (open, gated, secret, collapsed, flooded), some known only to some; cellars may have a way down, a thieves' den more likely. Nothing is torn down (silt, cave in, flood, brick up, seal; a growing town reopens before digging new); a catacomb never shrinks (ossuaries fill). Light: lamps, torches, braziers, daylight columns through gratings and shafts. Editing: two-point tunnel routes itself, drag, deepen, silt/reopen, streets into a ruin follow its grid, add a way down from any cellar (one undoable step), preview lists what an opening reaches.

render.instances). At every rung: at THORP, HAMLET, VILLAGE and at a TOWN whose draw left Features.sewers false, the tail runs T2 (ruin and cavern only - catacombs, quarries, vaults and the buried town keep TOWN and above - and the vaults step for a raised way's arch vaults and terminal cistern, which follow their way at every rung), T2b, T3's F6 only, T5 (L3, L5, L7), T6, T8, and T7 on show; never T1 or T4 as generators (no new network; undercity keeps II.7.5's rows); the village product shows the layer (V07).

Maintenance mode: at a village rung a system an earlier, larger rung left (V07's hand-off down: sewer network, catacomb, quarry, vaults, buried town) stays registered in maintenance mode: its stage re-derives its own part from its kept elements by corridorUnion (§4.11's rule for buried and dug parts), lays nothing new, never grows; U-FADE ages it at the underground rate; the foundation rule still collapses what a new footing meets; a catacomb keeps extentFloorM2, stagnant with blockedBy rung; an inherited undercity is re-read by UndercityEpoch.reread against the village row's bound 0 and vacates by II.7.5's rules, its chambers staying as host system elements; §3.5.0's TOWN gates bar only laying a new system; a replay runs the tail at the same fold position as generation (byte-for-byte, §6.2).

Standalone neighbourhood document (V1-3.10.1 step 6, (7)): S0 writes Features.sewers false and the undercity circumstance forbid (N0 commits nothing, P1-P4 forecast nothing, P6 no undercity, U-CITY never runs); in a hood document U-FORECAST runs after the one-district allocation, not before S7b (5), P7's cap reads that allocation's poorest-band households (J-V1.92), S7b (6)(d)'s void part from that allocation, P5's catacomb expectation ranks only the burial faces that allocation's anchors bring; Recipe.product read by this hood line (U-FORECAST at S7b and tail T2), its only reader besides S0; where 'hood', the tail runs the below-TOWN set whatever contextRung: T2 ruin and cavern (vaults only for a declared raised way's arch vaults and terminal cistern), T2b, T3's F6, T5's L3, L5, L7, T6, T8, T7 on show, plus U-SYS's catacomb step at TOWN's rules, chances and count one, candidates only the hood's own burial faces ((1) (a)-(d) inside the hood outline; never a quarry ossuary); no quarry, generated or forced vault or buried town; P5 and P7 forecast only ruin, cavern and the one catacomb; other rung-scaled rows read at the hood's contextRung (V1-2.6); a hood document runs no epoch in V06's first build (V1-3.10.1 (7)).

U-NET inputs: the rule families are II.6's; default family mixed (small streams culverted as trunks, mains under principal streets feeding them, all falling to the nearest admitted outfall downstream); constants NetworkRule (2.3) and the profile table (II.7.2). N0 gate and records: Features.sewers false -> U-NET commits nothing, part 0 schema-complete and empty (II.7.2); else mints the sewer UndergroundSystem on part 0, its rule naming the family and preset row (net.<family>.<preset>), writes part 0's L0 (margin ring = ground frame plus context margin §3.2 (9); rock face).

N1 service region R: ground districts (never sky) whose kind is not hinterland, underground or undercity (built extent intramural and extramural); a point is in R when pointLocate on the ground's L1 finds a face owned by one of them (§3.4).

N2 outfalls: candidates Terrain.outfalls with into in {river, sea, lake, canal, ditch} within outfall.reachM of R; admitted when downstream (II.7.2): on a river ContextVector.upstream >= 0.5 at Outfall.cell (read, never restated) and its course station s >= the station of every harbour basin's mouth and every water mill's intake on that course (outfall.below; a mill's intake station is the course station nearest its footprint centroid; a basin's mouth station the course station nearest the centroid of the basin face's edge shared with the river); on sea or lake at >= outfall.harbourClearM from every harbour basin face and the harbour-mouth chain's line (g 106 (e)); on a canal or ditch its flowTo end is beyond at. With none admitted, moat candidates admitted with start cost moatPenalty x reachM; with none of those, one field outfall: the D8 path of the hydro cell of largest accumulation on R's boundary followed outward to its first cell outside R and beyond the outermost enceinte's outer strip ({into field, water null, at that cell's centre snapped}). Every admitted candidate linked to the nearest way junction within outfall.linkM by a straight outfallRun edge; one with none dropped.

N3 drainage graph and tree: way edges = every way spine between consecutive junctions with an end within outfall.reachM of R's convex hull (extent fixed before the search), plus N2's outfall-run edges, each with spine polyline, class, and both directions' cost(u->v) = len x classCost[class] + adverseCostPerM x max(0, h_v - h_u) (sampler heights at end vertices, cm); pier and ford never carry a sewer; way edges ground part 0 only (a raised spine never an edge, never split, never a junction; the sewer follows the street under a viaduct); culvert edges (mixed, drainage-lines): every maximal D8 path of hydro cells in R whose catchment reaches culvertCatchHa outside every water face, polyline cell centres smoothed by chaikin passes, snapped, simplified at minEdge, directed downstream, cost len x culvertFactor; its end where it leaves R or enters water is an outfall node (a brook flowing on outside R ends at Outfall {into stream}); each crossing of a culvert with a way edge splits both at a new node; each way node within culvertLinkM of a culvert gains a link edge; drainage edges (drainage-lines only): the D8 tree on R's hydro cells, no way edge. follow-streets and mixed: multi-source Dijkstra (§3.1 binary heap) from admitted outfall nodes over reversed edges, heap keyed (cost, node address); drainage-lines: D8 itself; roots whose subtree drains < minOutfallHa dropped and the search re-run once; more than maxOutfalls[preset] -> largest subtrees kept, re-run once more; a node no root reaches drains by its gutters (area reported unsewered).

N3a declarations: (1) held runs (a drawTunnel without system, a locked or pinned run, a creation-prefix tunnel) enter the SewerGraph as fixed chains (centreline, kind, profile kept, cost 0, invert knots fixed); N7 treats them as constraints (a receiver's head takes min(own upper bound, held knot)); never re-laid, re-routed or truncated; (2) a user's delete of a generated run leaves a tombstone on its creation key in the network's derivation record: the way edges it followed take cost inf and N5 never re-selects them; (3) carry-over: regenerated runs matched by creation key (§6.3) keep depthOffsetCm, protected name and moved or edited access points (ground.at re-hosted by pointLocate); (4) SewerStrategy.extend and Re-derive from any stage read the same declarations.

N4 served area: each ground plot of R adds its area to the node nearer by station to the projection of its frontage midpoint on its Frontage.way edge; each edge adds its corridor area inside R (length inside R x way width) half to each end; under drainage-lines a plot adds to the hydro cell of its centroid; in reverse tree order served(n) = local(n) + sum served(child) in ha; edge n -> parent(n) carries served(n). N5 tunnel kinds: a culvert edge always culvert; a way or outfall-run edge carrying S ha is main when S >= mainMinHa[preset] and its class in classes[preset].main, drain when S >= drainMinHa[preset] and class in main union drain, else no tunnel; downstream closure: every edge on the tree path from a selected edge to its root selected, kind the greater of its own and upstream (drain < main; culvert stays culvert); an outfall run takes its incoming edge's kind; drainage-lines: drain at drainMinHa, main at mainMinHa, culvert at culvertCatchHa.

N6 runs and profiles: selected subgraph cut into runs at every node of degree != 2, every kind change, every change of the followed way and at outfall nodes; each run one Tunnel (II.6: one record, one condition); centreline = edges' polylines in flow order (a way run's positions read from the way's spine by resolve on the ground key, a copy of positions, never topology); follows the way (absent for culverts, drainage and outfall runs); widthCm and headroomCm from the profile table at (kind, preset), a historical main's by II.7.2's law with servedHa = served area at the run's downstream edge (in the derivation record, §2.8); navigable derived and stored; rule the row's id; a run reaching trunkHa is a named trunk. Wall crossings: where a centreline crosses a RetainingWall chain, two vertices inserted at the wall's two faces (chain offset by half the wall's thickness to its high and low side), each with levelledGroundCm on its own side; a way the wall turns into a stair or ramp keeps its spine, the run copies spine positions and adds these two; with no RetainingWall no vertex added and U-NET byte-identical.

N7 invert pass (every h = levelledGroundCm at the knot): (1) root-first: outfall knot floor low = h(at) + freeboardCm (the shore height standing for the water surface, as §2.6's water table reads it; mouth 30 cm above the water); a field outfall's = h(at) - coverMinCm - headroomCm; upstream low(v) = low(next) + minGradient x len(v, next); each knot starts at inv(v) = upper(v) = h(v) - coverCm - headroomCm + depthOffsetCm where upper(v) >= low(v), else at low(v) (cover shrinking below coverCm) admitted while the crown keeps coverMinCm (outfall run knots exempt: the mouth's cut through the bank), failing at v otherwise; (2) leaves-first: along each run inv(v) = min(inv(v), inv(prev) - minGradient x len(prev, v)); a run's head takes min(its invert, lowest downstream-end invert of runs entering it); held knots fixed; never lowers a knot below low(v); (3) drop at a wall: crossing high face to low face, the low-face knot starts at its own upper and the sweep's min makes the invert fall across the wall's thickness; the segment is a drop when its fall exceeds minGradient x its length: one run and one record (no junction), drawn as a drop shaft (5.2), exported with both knots; a run climbing a wall keeps falling, cover growing on the high side; no crown rises above the levelled ground at either face (T-V4-67). Crown depth h - inv - headroomCm <= coverMaxCm; F-NET ladder (BCR-7): (1) re-route: tree edge downstream of the first failing vertex cost inf, Dijkstra re-runs for nodes whose root path used it (<= maxReroute, no draw); (2) truncate: subtree above takes a local root if an admitted outfall lies within outfall.linkM of one of its nodes, else no tunnel, plots drain by gutter and pit, reported; terrain never lowered; an outfall knot unable to keep freeboard keeps it and reports W_OUTFALL_LOW; each vertex an invert_knot row; elevationCm = rounded mean invert; the sewer system's depthM = range of runs' crown depths.

N8 plot connections (serves): per plot of R (ground part 0), need = highest drain value among its uses' class rows (channel > pit > none), at least channel for an aqueduct terminal building's plot (overflow by the sewer; 3.5.4 (e)); II.7.1's table: channel -> nearest main or culvert run within reachM[preset] of its frontage midpoint (ties by address; the culvert is the mixed family's trunk), else where its class carries a drainPriority tag and a selected run's node lies within drainExtendM along its frontage way's spine, a drain run is added along that spine stretch (kind drain, invert by N7 from its head down to the receiver's invert, dropped if its head's crown exceeds coverMaxCm) and the plot connected, else unconnected, reported; pit -> one uniform on sewer keyed by the plot's lineage, connected to the nearest run within reachM when below the band's pitShareByBand (II.7.1), else unconnected silently; none -> never; a connection is logical (plot id in the run's sorted serves; no chain, no pin, no ground change).

N9 passages (navigable only): for every pair of navigable runs not sharing a junction whose centrelines come within passage.reachM in plan (uniform grid index), the closest points are a candidate when the network path between them is longer than passage.loopM; taken in order of (plan distance, sorted lineage), each run accepting at most floor(length / 1000 m x passage.perKm), a candidate crossing an accepted passage or with grade > passage.maxGrade refused; each accepted is a passage run (profile passage) splitting both mains at its ends (new junctions), invert linear between theirs.

N10 commit on part 0: one L1 batch inserts every run's centreline in address order as a tunnel chain with invert_knot rows; every vertex where >= 3 run ends meet takes a junction row and a Junction record (arms = the runs; chamber where navigable preset and >= chamberMinArms arms navigable); a kernel-found crossing between two unjoined runs is a junction too (§3.4), reported W_NET_CROSS, each run keeping its invert knots (the drop standing); every underground Junction takes kind as the ground does (§2.4): T, X or Y by arm count and angles, end at a dead end; one L2 batch runs corridorUnion over part 0's L1 faces with half-width widthCm/2 + wallCm (§3.7): half-band strips, junction wedges, rock between as part 0's blocks.

N11 network openings: on every main and culvert run, at its head where the head lies in R and every manholeSpacingM[preset] of centreline from it, the ground point above tested by pointLocate on ground part 0 (under a raised deck, on the way beneath): on public ground (1.2) an AccessPoint grating, role access, source system, knownTo public, state open; off public ground the site slides along the run in 5 m steps up to half the spacing each way, else skipped; each outfall takes a mouth (role access, ground.host the land face at at), each culvert's inlet where its brook enters R another; access_point vertices on the run's kerb at the nearest point (a part 0 transaction); cause {rule system, system the sewer}; a grating on a lived run is also the sewer-front neighbourhood's access (F5).

N11a grilles at walls: Tunnel.grilles is a view: stations where a run's band crosses an enceinte's wall_strip, a quay wall or a sea wall, found by a segment sweep at read; each draws as a gate bar across the band (5.2), exports as a closed VTT portal, public to the knowledge filter; an outfall run through a quay or sea wall keeps its mouth (no wall cuts off the water's access, g 106 (d)). N12 close: Features.underground true; report carries network length by kind, outfalls by into, connected share of plots by need, unsewered area, every F-NET use (§5.4).

U-FORECAST: NetworkForecaster.forecast(doc, rules) at S7b before (5) (hood document: after the one-district allocation) on what exists then (ways of S4, S5, district faces of S6, Terrain, roster of S2), gated: P1-P4 only where Features.sewers is true and for the chosen family; P5 and P7 at every rung for caverns and ruins and at TOWN+ for other kinds; P6 at TOWN+; hood document P5, P7 a ruin, a cavern and at most one catacomb. P1 = N1-N3 exactly on the same code (R from S6's districts); P2 served area from district faces (each district's L1 faces' area x dense core plot share 0.62, §4.2 S2, spread over bounding way edges by length, then N4 accumulation); P3 = N5, N6 (no N7) giving kind, profile, navigable; P4 admissible share: a way run's side strips lie under the street where halfWidth(way) - (widthCm/2 + wallCm) reaches the poorest band's minimum underground depth (II.7.3: 4 m x band row), else under frontage buildings (excluded): share = fraction of length under square faces or ways meeting that margin; a culvert or drainage run under blocks takes 1 - the district's coverage row; capacity = 2 x sum lengthM x admissibleShare / meanFrontage(poorest band) over navigable runs >= minRunM.

P5 voids (floor area / m2PerHousehold, II.7.5): ruin by its own existence and extent draws (U-SYS's keys) x forecastFloorShare 0.3; cavern by its existence draw and frame rock x maxRockShare x forecastFloorShare; vaults by part-0 bridges and steep ways (exact), forced vaults under require by their law (exact), never an arch vault or terminal cistern (no undercity takes them); buried town by the scar rule (exact); quarry by 3.5.3's volume law over the roster's predicted stone stock; catacombs (one expectation): roster's expected burial faces ranked by expected burials, first count of them, each need x face chance (hood: the one allocation's anchors' faces, the first). P6 undercity existence: II.7.5's rung row; TOWN draw = one uniform on sewer keyed (settlement, undercity), re-read by C0, never re-drawn; CircumstanceSlice.undercity (require -> exists at TOWN+ with n >= 1, forced vaults counted where no counted void qualifies; forbid -> none); size law H and n capped by counted voids' capacities in rank order (capacity x RuinRule.sourceWeight); returns {exists, n, H}. P7 chance of access (g 109 (j)): per forecast cavern or ruin void pAccess = 1 - (1 - pOpen) x prod_b (1 - pDig(b)) over buildings expected over its plan extent (each district face over it x coverage row x band's buildings per ha), each priced by DigRule at the ordinary house's class row and depthFactor at the void's top depth; pOpen = 1 - prod(1 - chance) over expected opening candidates; pAccess = 1 where a P3 run passes over the void within its depth range, and for a kind dug from the surface; a void counts toward P6 and F6 only when pAccess >= accessForecastMin 0.5; voidDwellingHouseholds = sum min(maxHouseholds, capacity) over counted cavern and ruin voids the undercity does not take, capped at voidDwellings.share x poorest band's households (hood: the allocation's). S7b (6),(7) allocate at most forecastSafety 0.85 x each forecast (BCR-19); advisory and deterministic, misses absorbed below (F0, C1) and the rest by T8, reported, never re-rolled; budget §12.4 row <= 3 ms CITY, <= 6 ms METROPOLIS, <= 1 ms village rung (BCR-11).

U-FRONT: II.7.3's rules (U1-U3, occupants, cut, surface constraint, access, depth, lifecycle, order) not restated; its steps: F0 gate and absorption: the underground Allocation exists (S7b (6)) and part 0 holds at least one open navigable run; with an allocation and no such run, households go first to other underground allocations with free capacity (an undercity neighbourhood, then F6's clusters), the remainder to T8, reported (F-SITING); a surplus S10b cannot seat on F2's plots raises occupancy of placed sewer-front cells in address order up to crowdCap per cell, the rest to T8. F1 frontages: each kerb edge of an open navigable run on each part-0 block is a frontage (II.7.3 cut (1)); a chamber junction's wedge never is (open floor; J-V4.9); Frontage records per block and run, class the run's kind.
