Fissures: 1 + floor(fissureMax x u) from rock cells of the frame's top slope decile (steepest first, >= tubeSpacingM apart), steepest line up to fissureMaxM, width fissureWidthCm, headroom fissureHeadroomCm (a draw per gallery), floor h - coverM - headroom capped by depthM, one or two breakdown chambers <= fissureChamberM2, never a hall. Openings are candidates (g 109 (j)(3)(ii)): crown cover < mouthCoverCm -> mouth candidate; breakdown chamber within skylightDepthM -> skylight; soluble chamber with cover < sinkholeCoverM under no footprint -> sinkhole; drawn by U-ACCESS (e); a failed mouth candidate ends its gallery sealed by talus; foundation rule applies.

Quarries: volume (II.7.6, J-A65.45) V = wasteFactor x (sum over stone buildings perimeter x (eaveCm - baseCm) x 60 cm + sum enceintes length x thicknessCm x heightCm + sum towers 0.4 pi r2 h); cells with SiteResources.stone >= 0.5 within reachM ordered (inside R first, stone value desc, distance to centre, cell index) until their volume reaches V; the surface quarry is §4.9's quarry land use without a source; a landfall's rubble working (a quarry with a source, V05 §3.16 (4), BCR-V5-26) is never the surface quarry, a stone working or a volume source; surface split: a taken cell of terrain class high (outcrop, cover < minCoverM) contributes its volume to §4.9's surface quarry, laid nowhere underground; other cells at headroom x (1 - pillarShare) per unit area grouped into workings (4-connected components; over workingMaxHa split along the OBB short axis); a working's floor = min_cells(h) - max(minCoverM + headroom, depthM.min) cm, a cell deeper than depthM.max dropped; layout: each working one workings chamber (outline cell union simplified at minEdge); room-and-pillar drawn not modelled (§8.2 quarry program: square pillars of side sqrt(pillarShare) x roomM at pitch roomM along the OBB axis); a public shaft (source system) on the nearest ground point within 30 m of the working's centre that is no footprint, access_point vertex on the chamber wall nearest below; workings joined by haulage galleries along a Euclidean Prim MST over centroids (ties index); the working nearest the town joined to its outcrop by an adit gallery ending in a mouth where the stone cell lies outside R.

Mine voids: same law on SiteResources.ore >= 0.5 cells, volume oreM3PerMine per mining class instance, in the quarry part. Chain mines (item 104 (h)(1), item 105): each ACTIVE chain whose resource node is subterranean reuses the nearest mine or quarry working within reachM or makes one at the hinterland edge on the nearest ore or stone cell of volume oreM3PerMine x chainVolume (low 0.5, moderate 1, high 2), its surface head the map feature item 104 (h)(1) places; the working is the chain's resource node (item 105); the undercity settles a workings chamber as any chamber (S10 cuts its floor, drawn pillars yielding to plots). Worked out: workedOut(working, scope?) a reading at every derivation, never stored: a mine working while its mining use is closed or gone; a chain mine while its chain is not ACTIVE; a stone working unless in the running epoch's scope.elements (at generation every stone working is worked out); readers 3.5.1 (1)(e), V06's candidate list (V6 §3.18.2 (1)), V10.

New workings at an epoch: QuarryWorkings.extend(doc, scope, epoch) (TOWN+; V06 under.extend after catacomb growth), one commit per kind: (1) stone: dV = wasteFactor x (volume law terms over scope.built's stone buildings and the enceinte stretches and towers the epoch's fortification step built), new cells in the volume law's order skipping cells under an existing working or the surface quarry's face, with the surface split, grouped into new workings; (2) mines: one working of oreM3PerMine per mining-class use whose opened epoch is this one, on ore cells in the same order; (3) chain mines: each ACTIVE chain with a subterranean resource node and no working; every existing working kept, never re-derived; each new working takes its workings chamber, shaft and one haulage gallery to the nearest existing working of its kind by centroid (ties index; none for the first), its ordinal the system's next unused (no renumbering), joins EpochScope.elements; its commit runs U-ACCESS (a)'s overlap test and, for a mine working, the mine breach; where cells within reachM run out before dV, the rest from the surface quarry, unmet m3 reported; no draw.

Vaults (a) bridge vaults: each deck end of a built part-0 Bridge deck over water (never a raised deck) whose deckCm stands more than bridgeRiseCm over the bank's ground takes one bridgeVault chamber under its approach way (corridor over approachM from the deck end, inset 50 cm, floor vaultBelowCm below the street, ceiling 300); (b) street vaults: every part-0 way stretch >= 12 m in R whose along-way grade exceeds vaultSlope takes a streetVault under its corridor (inset 50 cm, floor vaultBelowCm below the stretch's lowest street point), the grade measured over the way's ramped profile with stair intervals left out (a stair where a way crosses a RetainingWall is no vault source; a raised ramp never a street-vault stretch); (c) cisterns: each growth-stage-1 precinct and the castle where min(dist.water, plan distance to the nearest aqueduct delivery point) > cisternDistM takes a cistern under its open court (a yard part; the castle's inner ward or bailey face), rounded square of the row's area, floor cisternBelowCm below, a well access in the court above; a cistern record forces one; aqueductDelivery(doc) = each aqueduct's terminal point and every public fountain it feeds (BCR-45), reading only the base's eager aqueduct records, the base's aqueduct need test reading none of V04's cisterns (no cycle; J-V4.83); II.7.3's surface list binds every vault of (a)-(c) and (e), the cistern's own host admitted (BCR-20); each street or bridge vault takes a stair from the corridor at its downhill end, source system, knownTo public.

Arch vaults (g 110 (b)): the base fixes each span's use eagerly (BCR-45), V04 reads it, never decides it; ArchVaults.reconcile(doc, raised, cause) visits each raised way of raised (every one at T2) in address order: (1) lay: each span of use vault has one chamber, kind archVault, key (arch, way lineage, a, b), span its SpanKey, found by key or created; footprint the span's under-deck rectangle between the piers' inner faces (the deck's plan outline on ground part 0) inset archInsetPierCm 60 at the piers and archInsetOpenCm 30 at the two open faces; floor elevationCm = levelledGroundCm at the span's axis midpoint, levelled and cut into the uphill side; ceiling the span's soffit (BCR-45) less that floor; one door AccessPoint (source system, knownTo public, cause {system: the vaults system}, ground.host the part-0 face at its point) at the midpoint of the open face whose archDoorStripM 2 m strip beyond holds the most part-0 way or open ground (no footprint, no water), ties lower side index; neither face opens -> no door, W_ARCH_VAULT_NO_DOOR (a walled-up arch); (2) condition: closure follows its span each reconcile: collapsed where the span's state is ruined or cleared, where its V06 condition reads breached or dismantled (BCR-V6-26), or a bounding support's state is ruined or cleared (f item 244), a landfall's ruin included (V05 §3.16 (4)); else none; U-FADE never strikes it; (3) remove: every arch vault whose span no longer exists or whose use is open, and every arch vault of a way no longer in the model, deleted with its door, links and accesses in the same commit, each a dry-run fate; chambers in the vaults system's part (created at the first), one L1 batch and one L2 corridorUnion per reconcile; not undercity voids (P5, C1, forced vaults, U-FRONT, F6, U-FADE exclude them; L3 and U-DIG's connector never target one; U-ACCESS (b)'s proximity links reach it as any vaults element); §8.2's chamber row reads it as storage (vault hatch); an institution stands in one only by declaration (T6 place inside its footprint, a skeleton placeAt): the use on one plot equal to the chamber's floor and one single-storey building under its ceiling, entrance at the door, faces by the ground the door opens onto (§2.6); V03 plans it as any building.

Terminal cistern (e): an aqueduct whose terminal kind is cistern (BCR-45) takes one cistern chamber keyed (terminal, aqueduct lineage) under the yard part of its terminal building's plot (V11 conduit_house, V2 §3.17 (b)) where one stands, else under the public ground nearest the terminal point; rounded square of terminalCisternM2 600 m2, floor cisternBelowCm below, a well access in the yard or on the public ground above (source system, cause {system}); the terminal building's plot drain need at least channel (N8); where neither yard nor public ground takes it, it shrinks in 10 % steps down to the precinct cistern's 150 m2, else skipped, W_TERMINAL_CISTERN_SKIPPED; the aqueduct's buried stretches stay the base's line on ground part 0, never an underground system; they are foundation obstacles (3.5.0).

Buried old town: II.7.6's rule, region the growth-stage-1 districts; galleries those districts' way centrelines (old streets under the new), storey chambers their buildings' footprints, and each square of the region (L1 square face or square block) a square chamber (BCR-20: the old market under the new); floors at scarBaseCm + scarGainCm x severity below the present grade; headrooms and ceilings by the 3.5.0 table; a building's entrance vertices kept on its storey chamber's wall as portal rows for exports; the same builder serves raiseGrade at an epoch or by hand over the raised region's records. Terraces under a raised grade: floors follow the old grade point by point (levelledGroundCm on the region's last live state before the raise, less the rule's depth); a RetainingWall the same batch tombstones inside the region (cause convert:raiseGrade, V6 §3.19.4 (1)) is a step in the buried floor: elements on its high side keep the high side's datum (the step = V01 stepProfile, BCR-43, on that last live state at the nearest station); a gallery crossing the wall's line takes two knots at the wall's faces (as N6), the segment a stair step (one gallery and record, drawn as a stair); a square chamber the line crosses split along it, each side at its own datum; with no wall nothing changes; a buried town is reachable by construction (the raised town's cellars open into its old storeys): excavation always accessible.

Forced vaults: where CircumstanceSlice.undercity = require and P6 finds no counted void with capacity for one neighbourhood, U-SYS lays a vaults complex under the oldest district (lowest growthStage, then largest area, ties address), after the ordinary vaults: a grid of streetVault chambers of forcedGridM 8 m pitch under that district's public ground (ground part 0 by pointLocate), never within reach of a foundation obstacle and never counting or joining an arch vault, at the vault row's floor vaultBelowCm, joined by vault galleries along the grid, grown breadth-first from the district's largest square of either kind (else its centroid's nearest corridor) until floor area reaches max(minHouseholds, H) x m2PerHousehold, plus one market chamber of mainChamberM2 at the grid's start; the shallow-element rule binds it; where the ground cannot take it the complex steps its floor below surfaceClearCm (the surface rule then releases it) and grows again, so C1's 'none formed' cannot occur under require (T-V4-37); under forbid S7b (7) makes no allocation and U-CITY does not run.

U-ACCESS (a) overlap and mine breaches (T2b, after U-SYS, before U-FRONT; every link and access records its cause): overlap: for every pair of elements of different parts whose plan bands intersect and whose vertical intervals (floor to floor plus headroom or ceiling) intersect, one link at the intersection's centroid, via breach, cause overlap, naming the growing system and event; where one end is a sealed cavern or ruin element its kind is open (owner's rule), else from LinkRule.kinds, a builders' grille reading gated; neither element moves (the sewer's course and hydraulics never bent); where plan bands intersect and the vertical gap is > 0 and <= overlapShaftM 6 m, a shaft link with overlapShaftChance 0.1 (a uniform keyed by the pair, no epoch component). Mine breach: a mine working whose wall lies within breachM 40 m in 3-D of a cavern gallery joins it by a heading gallery in the quarry part along the straight 3-D segment (floor graded at most digMaxGrade, a stair link where steeper), with a breach link of kind open, cause mineBreach, at the cavern end (the working's shaft the cave's access by transitivity). Village working: at a village rung with no quarry system, each mining use's outside-plot working (at T2b every one; with a scope those in scope.workings) tested against cavern and ruin elements whose plan band lies within breachM of the working's plot ring and whose top lies at most the working's mine.workingDepthM (V07: open cast 10 m, shaft 30 m) below levelledGroundCm at the plot's centroid; the nearest such element of each void system (plan distance, ties address) takes an AccessPoint at the working (shaft, role access, source dig, knownTo local, state open, ground.host the working's plot face, ground.at its pole of inaccessibility, access_point vertex on the element's kerb or wall nearest below), cause {mineBreach, system, event}, no link record; keyed (working lineage, element lineage), idempotent, no draw; at V07's hand-off up the working becomes a quarry source and the access is kept. The same overlap test runs wherever a system grows (SewerStrategy.extend, catacomb growth, new quarry, mine or chain working, U-DIG passages, a lifeline, an edit that draws or deepens an element), each in its own commit, recording its cause.

U-ACCESS (b) proximity links: for each pair of parts (a < b) and each element e of part a (tunnels, galleries, chambers, open or closed), samples every 5 m of its centreline or outline query part b's static index for elements within linkReachM in plan whose floor lies within linkDepthM; per element pair stations taken greedily along e, each at least linkSpacingM beyond the last and beyond any (a) link; at each one uniform on sewer keyed (two elements' lineages, station ordinal) against the pair of kinds' chance (II.7.6); kind by weights, flooded only where both floors lie below the water table; via by floor difference: <= 100 cm breach (door where an end is an underground building's wall), <= 300 cm stair, else shaft; knownTo by II.7.6 (4); cause proximity; two link_end vertices on each element's kerb or wall at the nearest points, one transaction per part (§3.4).

U-ACCESS (c) crypt joins: a church-class building on ground part 0 (never sky; crypt column always or basement) with Basement.crypt (BCR-V3-20: derived with the basement at S11, exists at generation without any plan elaborated) whose crypt ring lies over a catacomb element in plan or within accessReachM 5 m of one draws once per (church, complex) pair: one uniform on sewer keyed by the pair (one mixer over the church's and complex source's lineages), no epoch component (a join first reached by an epoch's growth gives the answer a regeneration gives); chance cryptJoin.own 0.7 when the complex's source is the church's own churchyard, else cryptJoin.other 0.3; success makes an AccessPoint from the crypt, source crypt, cause {crypt, system}: kind door where the element's floor lies within stairDropCm of the crypt floor, else cellar_stair; head stays in the crypt (V03 AccessHostRow catacomb with cause crypt -> crypt); the join replaces item 64's draw for that pair; a building without Basement.crypt draws nothing; a church-class building's only way to a catacomb is this join (L3 gives it no basement access to a catacomb element; no system catacomb access headed in it); catacomb galleries under a church keep foundationClearM below its basement floor; a crypt is joined only by this access, never cut.

U-ACCESS (d) dig from above: every ground building (ground part 0; a raised-way pier is no building) whose footprint overlaps in plan a cavern or ruin element whose top lies below the building's dig floor (basement floor = baseCm less Basement.floors x cellar.depthCm, §2.6, where it has a basement, else baseCm), or whose basement ring lies within DigRule.planReachM 5 m in plan of one, draws once per void kind: one uniform on sewer keyed (building lineage, dig, void kind), no epoch component (the building's lineage carries its epoch); p = min(cap 0.6, classRow(class) x basementFactor (1.5 with a basement, 1 without) x depthFactor(d)); depthFactor 1 for d <= reachM 6 m, exp(-(d - reachM)/decayM 2 m) beyond, 0 beyond maxM 20 m; d the vertical distance from dig floor to the element's top; success -> an AccessPoint to the shallowest such element under the footprint, source dig, cause {dig, system, event}: cellar_stair where it has a basement and the drop lies within stairDropCm, else a shaft, and a well where the plot's well pin stands over the element; head in the basement (V03's access head); evaluated at every derivation but its value fixed by key: an access once made persists (removed only by 3.10's host closures), one not yet made appears when the building's chance later rises above its draw (basement added, deeper void reached); a building never draws twice for one kind; item 109 (d)'s chance raised over a ruin is this row.

U-ACCESS (e) public openings: each candidate of 3.5.2 and 3.5.0a (sinkhole, mouth, skylight, collapsed_shaft over a quarry, mine or ruin chamber under a square, a square or green block or a field face with cover <= 15 m, ruin_entrance at the ruin's marker) draws its OpeningRow.chance: one uniform on sewer keyed (candidate element lineage, opening kind), no epoch component, never re-drawn; success makes an AccessPoint of that kind (BCR-29), source opening, role access (a skylight is a mouth of role light), cause {opening, system}, knownTo public (a ruin_entrance local unless the dossier says the ruin is known).

U-ACCESS (f) reuse: an element adopted by another system keeps its place, part and kind and takes reusedBy {system, since} (BCR-33) with one link of cause reuse, via breach, at the adopting system's nearest element; the adopter counts its area in its extent and draws it with its own program as an overlay (nothing laid twice); the sewer adopts an ancient drain after the fact: a ruin main street carrying its drain takes reusedBy the sewer where a laid run's centreline lies within reuseM 3 m of it for at least 30 m, its floor falls in the run's flow direction at >= minGradient, and its crown depth is at most coverMaxCm (the run keeps its record and course); a catacomb's tomb reuse and the quarry ossuary's adoption made by U-SYS and recorded the same way; a well pin whose shaft (to the water table plus 100 cm) passes through a ruin or cavern chamber is always an access (kind well, source dig, cause dig) at every rung (V07's village well and pump pins are this pin record, V07 §3.16 (3)(ii)); a buried chamber within linkReachM above a ruin chamber takes a stair link at the any-buried chance.

U-ACCESS (g) excavation reading: excavation(cluster) is accessible or unexcavated for every cluster (connected component of a part's open galleries and chambers joined at junctions and chamber walls) of a cavern or ruin part; connection graph nodes = clusters of every part and the surface; edges = links of kind open, gated or secret and access points in state open or locked; a cluster is accessible when the graph joins it to the surface (transitively); any other part kind always accessible (sewer, catacombs, quarries, vaults, dug passages dug from the surface; the buried town entered from the cellars above); derived, never stored: union-find over clusters recomputed after every commit touching an access, a link, an element's closure or a building over a void, for the clusters it touches, cached by the underground's digest; V12's undergroundInputOf reads it as state unexcavated.

Access-pass determinism: item 64's basement draw stays in U-LINK (T5); dig draws are U-ACCESS's; the two stages' stream keys differ by stage id (§6.1), within U-ACCESS each (building, void kind) has its own salt (no draw depends on another rule's presence); keys in 3.12. With a scope: AccessPass.run(doc, scope?) without scope (T2b) runs (a)-(g) over the whole document; with V06's scope (under.access, afterGrowth 20) runs (a), (b), (f) over scope.elements and (a)'s village-working test over scope.workings, (c) for pairs whose catacomb element is in scope.elements, (d) for buildings of scope.built and scope.basementGrown, (e) for candidates among scope.elements and under faces of scope.surfaceChanged, then (g); every step idempotent (a link or access found by its creation key kept, never made twice), each made access or link records event = the epoch's seq; last step V01's opening pass over the public openings (e) made.

U-CITY: existence, size law, allocation, shadow rules, outskirts and light are II.7.5's; layout constants UnderLayoutRule. C0 existence: re-reads P6's verdict {exists, n, H}, never re-draws; the four requirements checked on the built voids; under require at least one neighbourhood forms (3.5.6 lays its void where none is counted), the first takes the Underground city record's assignment (District.identity.dossier = the record's binding key, name the record's name, a protected dossier name, never a naming-slice draw); under forbid U-CITY does not run.

C1 the voids read-only first: for each built system part whose kind the preset admits (UndercityRule.presets; historical admits ruin, BCR-42), clusters = connected components of open galleries and chambers (joined at junctions and chamber walls), arch vaults and the terminal cistern excepted; a cavern or ruin cluster a candidate only while accessible (the undercity never excavates a sealed void); capacity = floor area (chambers plus bands of galleries carrying no water; a water gallery counts 0, is never a walkway, still joins clusters and serves as a water lifeline) / m2PerHousehold; each candidate passes a read-only lifeline test before any commit (L1's candidate search for access, air, water and C2's carve feasibility against the parts after U-ACCESS; a failing cluster is not a candidate, so no neighbourhood is dropped after commit); ranked by capacity x RuinRule.sourceWeight[kind]; where a ruin and another kind both qualify the first pick is one draw on sewer keyed (settlement, undercityRank) weighted by those products (V12's ruinChosen share = w_ruin / sum w), the rest in descending product, ties lowest address; one neighbourhood each while fewer than n formed and the cluster holds >= minHouseholds; where fewer clusters qualify than n and the largest holds >= 2 x householdsPerNeighbourhood it is split in two by its chamber graph (seeds the two chambers farthest apart by graph distance, each node to the nearer, ties address; no draw); H shared by capacity, each capped at its own; none formed (never under require): households to the pseudo-district's free capacity (sewer-front plots, then F6) and the remainder to T8, reported (F-VOID); under require where the counted void proves sealed, the required neighbourhood takes it with a lifeline stair of cause dossier.

C2 main chamber: the core (District.core) is in order a ruin court, temple or hall chamber of at least mainChamberM2 (an ancient forum first, g 109 (e)); else the cluster's largest chamber >= mainChamberM2; else carved by U-CITY's carve post-pass on the host part: from the cluster node nearest its area centroid (ties address) a 16-gon of radius sqrt(mainChamberM2/pi) + carveMarginM inserted as a chamber_wall chain of kind market, floor the seed's, ceiling by 3.5.0's table; a ruin chamber holding a monument is a core candidate where its floor less the monument's tier-0 ring and mound reaches mainChamberM2 (the monument stands inside the plaza disc, kept clear by stall pins and walkways); the carve lays nothing within reach of a foundation obstacle; each host gallery crossing the 16-gon split at the wall by §6.3's SPLIT rule, inside parts existence cleared, cause rule:undercity-carve, kept never deleted; a New random on the host system re-runs the carve for every neighbourhood whose core it held (same transaction set); a New random on the neighbourhood resurrects the cleared parts (§2.8) and re-carves; carve feasibility (admitted area inside the part's depth band and clear of other clusters' elements reaching carveMinShare of mainChamberM2) is part of C1's test.

C3 streets: the core's plaza = disc of radius sqrt(plazaShare x area / pi) about its centroid ringed by a closed walkway (Gallery with walkway, width walkwayCm, wall 0): plots front the ring's outer kerb, disc stays open; in every chamber >= walkwayMinChamberM2 the openings (gallery-wall meeting vertices, access points) and one hub (the ring's nearest point for the core, the centroid otherwise) joined by a Prim MST (ties index) whose edges are shortest paths inside the chamber polygon (visibility graph on its vertices; a monument's standing rings and mound, a foundation pillar and each column point grown to 60 cm are holes), each edge a walkway; every cluster gallery joining two chambers of the neighbourhood and carrying no water takes walkway (II.7.5's adopted streets); one L1 batch, one L2 corridorUnion batch.

C4 plots and buildings: S10 on the neighbourhood's blocks with frontages on walkway and gallery kerbs and chamber walls (II.7.5); the shallow-element surface test through F-UNDER's samples where the ceiling lies within the host row's surfaceClearCm (blocks recording ground cells as F3); no plot on a floor at or below the water table; no plot on a monument's standing tiers or mound or a foundation pillar (obstacles cut out), while a plot may hold column points (V03 §3.12 (6) plans round them); every entrance S11 derives here takes Entrance.faces tunnel (BCR-V3-21); S10b places the neighbourhood's share with relation families by underDistance, the black market as a hard near: core row fronting the ring (bound to a Black market bazaar record where the dossier holds one); ladder members, SIZE steps and clandestine modes as F4; no crypt ever seated below; S11 with UndercityRule.arrangements, heights ceiling-capped (II.7.5); the ring's stall pins by §4.7's market pins at the secondary-market scale. C5 the district: District {kind undercity, parent, core, faces} with II.7.5 (2)'s parent rule computed as the first entry of V01 districtsAbove(part, core) (V1-3.16); prosperity field as II.7.5 states (parent's field with its daylight term); outskirts written by L6 (BCR-4). C6 lights by 3.9's undercity rows.

Cross-arena distance: underDistance(member, target) for a member on an underground part = shortest path over the member's part's open walkways, galleries, chamber floors and tunnels (and on through open links into other parts) to an open access point or lifeline whose knownTo the member's use admits (public use: public and local accesses; clandestine: its own knownTo and wider) plus the ground's street-mode distance (§4.7) from that access's ground.at to the target; an underground target takes the underground path where shorter (II.7.5 (3) built); SUPPLY, CLIENTELE, COMPETITION, item 105's links and item 107's comfort distance read it for underground members; EMITS and SENSITIVE-TO act within an arena only (rock absorbs smell, smoke, noise) except water pollution reaching the ground at the network's outfalls (a sewer-front tannery counts at its run's outfall) and disorder reaching the parent district; ALIGNMENT reads plan distance (a guild seat under the garrison still repels, item 103 (b)); coverage (item 103): each undercity neighbourhood and the underground pseudo-district is a catchment for the everyday-service classes whose V11 row admits the arena; item 103 (e)'s siting statistics run on underground members against a random-placement baseline (T-V4-60).

L1 lifelines realised (II.7.5 (4)): for each undercity neighbourhood in address order L1 makes what C1's test found: access (accessible by construction; where its nearest access is another part's element, L1 writes that lifeline link: kind open, or secret by lifelineSecretShare, a draw on sewer keyed by the district, via by U-ACCESS (b)'s floor rule, cause lifeline; where a basement access is cheapest L1 creates it with source lifeline, cause lifeline, and L3 skips that building; else the shallowest element's ground point above on ground part 0 (public ground or a yard, or outside ground: under a raised deck on the way beneath, never inside a raised-way pier's footprint) within lifelineReachM: a stair where the drop <= stairMaxDepthCm else a shaft, source lifeline, knownTo secret by the same draw else local); air (a grating of role air on public ground above a walkway or chamber, else a well pin's point, else a ruin decoration's, else a shaft through a building whose footprint lies over the cluster (its chimney), one per neighbourhood and one more per airPerM2 of floor); water (a water gallery or cistern of the cluster or linked within linkReachM, else a well pin within 30 m in plan (a well access), else a river-bank mouth of a cavern of the cluster); a route outside (satisfied when the graph reaches a mouth or outfall, never required); a realisation that cannot place a vertex the test found runs U-DIG's lifeline closure from the district ring, pieces keyed (district lineage, piece ordinal), target never an unexcavated cluster; no neighbourhood dropped here. L2 links between parts are U-ACCESS (b)'s, run before the undercity. L4 lifeline closures run inside L1.

L3 basement accesses (item 64): II.7.3's Basement accesses (1)-(5), building by building on ground part 0 (never sky) in address order, cause {basement}, for every target but a cavern or ruin element (U-ACCESS (d) decides those), a catacomb element from a church-class building (the crypt join is its only way) and an arch vault (at grade, by the street), skipping a building L1 gave a lifeline access; runs after U-FRONT and U-CITY since its targets include sewer dwellings' and undercity buildings' walls and walkways (II.7.3 (1)).

L5 subterranean dossier institutions: an institution with facets.subterranean that S10b placed on a surface plot has a basement (S10b's hard row admits only plots whose terrain gate allows one; S11 forces it by the requested-mode ladder, BCR-43) and takes the first rung that succeeds: (1) a basement access to the nearest element within accessReachM; (2) U-DIG's connector to an element within digReachM; (3) U-DIG's minimal dug system to an outlet; (4) always: a cellar chamber of the dug system directly beneath its basement (floor at the dug row's upper depth, cellar 6 m2, knownTo the institution's, no connector) reached by a hatch - where the water table lies above that floor the chamber is created flooded and W_SUBTERRANEAN_WET reported; an Underground network record takes the dug network instead (2.3a); every L5 piece keyed (institution binding key, piece ordinal) on sewer, source system with the building among the dug system's sources, cause dossier, held while the institution is live (4.4); the rung used reported (T-V4-34). L6 outskirts: from each link endpoint on part 0 joining a neighbourhood's cluster, a walk along open part-0 runs up to outskirtsReachM; the U-FRONT blocks whose frontage runs it reaches are District.outskirts (II.7.5); re-run after any part-0 edit within outskirtsReachM of a lifeline link. L7 close: Features.underground recomputed (II.7.4).

T8 U-RECONCILE (last eager tail stage): inputs what the tail could not seat below after absorption (F0, C1, F6): surplus households and institutions no underground plot took (an underground-mode concealed use; an undercity preferred or underground preferred class); households by S10b's reconcile (§4.7) to the ground's vacant residential buildings of the poorest band (first in the parent district of the neighbourhood meant for, else the district above their run, else the town's poorest district), then to occupied poorest-band buildings up to each building's capacity (§4.7 generation fill), address order; a remainder reported in requestedVsBuilt and still counted in the population; institutions take item 63's chain (§4.7 Concealed institutions (2): underground -> front -> hidden) or their class row's ground placement by S10b's reconcile on a vacant ground plot; T8 writes uses and household counts only (no plot, face, footprint or building created, moved or removed; ground geometry and digests stay first paint's; T12-1's 0 writes on the ground PlatKey holds); besides T8 the tail writes ground records only in T6's S13a step (V01's opening places); the ground's model digest finalised after T8; every T8 write reported; T-V4-3 bars its rate (<= 2 % of CITY seeds at default presets).

U-DIG (pieces and order II.7.6's, closure mechanics §7.3 item 9's): target search: each part's static index queried for elements within accessReachM of the basement ring (direct access, no connector), then within digReachM, in II.7.6's order, ties plan distance then address; an arch vault never a target; from a church-class building a catacomb element only as a hand crypt join (4.1). Connector: a local grid of digGridCm cells over the bounding box of basement ring and target point grown by 20 m (at most 400 x 400 cells; larger a refusal naming the bound); step cost = step length x rockCost of the terrain class (damp and flood infinite); infinite within foundationClearM of every other building's footprint and basement ring, within reach of every foundation obstacle, within every dug passage's band, under a water face, and where the water table lies above the passage floor; A* with octile heuristic x least cost, ties (f, g, cell index); path cell centres simplified (Visvalingam at minEdge) and snapped; floor falls linearly from basement floor to target floor clamped to the dug row's depth range, 30 cm above the water table and below the network's coverCm (II.7.2); a remaining drop beyond digMaxGrade taken by the end link's stair (via); a route longer than 2 x digReachM a refusal with reason (II.7.6). Minimal system: nothing within digReachM -> the outlet row's first kind with a candidate within 2 x digReachM (another cellar of the same Use.owner, a void, the nearest river or canal bank, the shore, the nearest point beyond the outermost enceinte's outer strip) ends the passage: a mouth on outside ground or a door into the other cellar.

U-DIG keys: an edit's pieces keyed by the event's seq (§7.3 item 9 (b)); a lifeline's at generation by (district lineage, piece ordinal); L5's by (institution binding key, piece ordinal); each on sewer; generated pieces re-derive with their owner (neighbourhood New random; institution relocation); edit-made pieces held (§7.3 item 9 (c)); a regenerate on the dug system re-derives only generated pieces, dry run listing held ones as kept (BCR-24). Voids and bans: target search never picks an element of an unexcavated cluster unless the edit names it, or the access is BCR-V9-22's grouped access (base §7.3 item 9 (d) as f item 372 applies it): an addUndergroundAccess {building} with no target grouped before a dwelling declaration on an unexcavated cluster (V9 §4.17.4) targets that cluster's element nearest in plan to the building's footprint (ties address); either is the user's excavation (cause edit), dry run listing the clusters it opens; the declaration's closure then finds the cluster reachable and adds no access; the grouped access keeps every other piece of its own closure (basement by §2.6's requested-mode ladder, connector where the target lies beyond accessReachM, plan reservation); rule holds for a building the dwelling closure's first rung qualifies, an untargeted access from any other building takes the ordinary search; forbiddenResources make damp and flood infinite.

Dwelling closure's way in (base §7.3 item 9 (d) as f item 372 applies BCR-V9-22; V9 §4.17.4): a dwelling declaration on an unexcavated cluster (a quarter or drawBoundary on a void part, a placeAt of a dwelling class on a void plot, a clerk's proposal) is a closure whose first rung calls U-DIG: buildings above the cluster = ground buildings (never a raised-way pier) that 3.5.7 (d)'s geometry admits over one of its elements (footprint overlapping in plan or basement ring within DigRule.planReachM), each measured to the cluster's element nearest in plan (ties address); one qualifies when its dig floor lies within DigRule.maxM above that element's top; ordered by plan distance then address; the first digs: target that element (a reused piece), pieces U-DIG's connector only where the element lies beyond accessReachM of the basement ring (or footprint without a basement), the access and the plan reservation, no basement piece (the building as it stands), no minimal system; access of (d)'s kinds (cellar_stair with a basement and drop within stairDropCm, else shaft; well where the well pin stands over the element), head by V03's access head, source dig, cause {edit, system: the cluster's system, event: the declaration's seq}, with bend.under.accessDug; a building whose connector U-DIG refuses (2 x digReachM or no finite path) passed over, listed in the dry run with reason; the rung fails only when none remains; dry run lists in PreviewResult.alternatives the qualifying buildings after the one that dug, at most three, without digging them; a re-preview of the grouped access from one whose connector is then refused is refused with reason (§7.3 item 9 (e)); second and third rungs (a public opening at the nearest (e) candidate with chance waived, else a collapsed_shaft at the base's point of public ground over the cluster) made by U-ACCESS (e)'s opening maker as placeAccess's public-opening form (source opening, role access, cause {edit, system, event}, knownTo by (e)'s rule, V01's opening pass in the same commit); fourth (bend onto ground part 0) the base's; pieces keyed by the declaration's seq, recorded in its closure record, held while live, removed by its undo; the excavation reading opens the cluster in the same commit; in a skeleton prefix the closure runs where U-CITY C0 reads the declaration on a cluster still unexcavated after T2b (4.7), a grouped access before it running there first rather than among T5's closures (J-V4.120). Edit-triggered lifeline closure (§7.3 item 9 (d); C4-42): after the dry run of a drawBoundary or split on an undercity district, C1's read-only lifeline test runs for each resulting district; a failing one calls the lifeline generators from its ring, keyed by its lineage and the event's seq, pieces shown as fates on T5 and T9.

Underground light rows (model §8.4: no global light, ambient.underground, shafts, hand lantern; arena underground, §4.7 LightRule, extension, own values; placed by the engine making the host; magic = admitted circumstance values (BCR-39 lets it include none); a row without magic lights under every value): sewer and F6 door (band's fuel, fire; 170 cm, 6 cd, radius 500, size 3; one per entrance); sewer tunnel junction (torch, fire; 220, 15, 800, 5; one per junction of a lived run, host the arm of lowest address); sewer accessPoint (torch; 220, 12, 700, 5; one per access of a lived run); undercity door (band's fuel; 180, 10, 700, 5); undercity door of tavern, fence, guild seat, shrine, pit, healer (lantern; 250, 25, 1000, 8; one per main entrance); undercity walkway gallery (torch; 230, 15, 900, 5; spacing solved by §4.7 (2) for minLux poor 0.5, modest 0.8, prosperous 1.2 lx; magic none, low); walkway (magical orb, magic; min(500, ceiling - 30), 30, 1200, 30; torch spacing x 1.5; magic high); market chamber (brazier; 100, 60, 1400, 25; ceil(area/150 m2) on the ring's inner kerb by arc length); other chamber >= 400 m2 (fire pit; 30, 40, 1200, 25; ceil(area/400) at hubs); catacomb ossuary chamber (shrine lamp; 120, 3, 400, 5; one per ossuary); catacomb entrance (shrine lamp; one); cavern gallery (glow fungus, magic; 20, 0.5, 300, 30; every 15 m where magic is low or high or the biome is temperate_forest, wetland, jungle (V11 reviews)); ruin hall or temple chamber (ancient glow, magic; ceiling - 30, 8, 900, 20; ceil(area/300), each chamber with magicLightChance 0.5 drawn on sewer keyed by the chamber; magic low, high); ruin accessPoint (torch; one per access of a lived cluster); quarry, vaults, buried accessPoint (torch; one per access of a lived system, an arch vault's door excepted).

Fuel: a door row's band's fuel by the plot's band and the era row: poor rushlight (6 cd, size 3), modest tallow lamp (8 cd, size 4), prosperous and above oil lamp (10 cd, size 5); an era row may replace them (V11); a run, system or cluster is lived when it carries plots (F6 included) or lies within litReachM 60 m of one; an unlived network or system is dark but for its shafts; an unexcavated cluster carries no light; every underground light's height capped at its host's ceiling - 30 cm; door sides drawn on pin.light as on the ground (§4.7 (4)); arch vaults carry no light row (daylit through the door, treated by the light pass as §8.4 (b)'s shaft with the archDoor opening row); a declared institution in one takes the sewer door row's lamp by its band's fuel.

Epoch callers: the evolution engine owns the epoch; V04's parts it calls (BCR-6), usable by hand now; V06 schedules them (links' re-binding, excavation, ruin decay, catacomb growth); callers = V06's four participants (V6 §3.2): under.fade at decline (10) runs UndergroundFade; under.extend at afterGrowth (10) runs Foundations.apply over the epoch's scope, then the arch-vault reconcile, then SewerStrategy.derive the first epoch Features.sewers turns on (else .extend with its wall drops), then CatacombGrowth.grow with opts, then QuarryWorkings.extend; under.access (20) runs AccessPass.run(doc, scope); under.undercity (30) runs UndercityEpoch.reread then F6 (new dwellings filled by V06's relocation); on the grow-by-stage path V04's own M4 hooks call the same functions without V06's scope and opts.

UndergroundFade.candidates(doc, epoch): every tunnel, gallery and chamber neither locked nor pinned (an arch vault excepted: its condition follows its span), in use, neglected or partly caved in, whose dwell band has run (§4.11: tunnels two bands slower than a building, from its last condition change), weight w = E_u x rate(underground) x u x neglect: E_u mean of §4.11's exposure field over the ground points above the element every sampleM (II.6); rate the underground persistence row 0.03; u the underground lottery's draw on epoch.transform keyed (element lineage, epoch); neglect = 1 + neglectGain x (1 - usage), usage in [0,1] = share of a run's served and fronting plots occupied, of a lived system's plots occupied, 1 for a catacomb whose burial face is open (stagnant included) and 0 closed, 1 for a vault whose way is live, a ruin cluster's its dwellings' occupancy (0 while unexcavated), 0 for an unlived cavern or quarry; a ruin element's weight x RuinRule.fadeFactor. UndergroundFade.apply(element, epoch): the op drawn on epoch.transform from UndergroundFadeRule.ops at its class and condition, seal weight x (1 + orderGain x (1 - disorder)); a run longer than 120 m struck on a 120 m stretch centred at its most exposed sample (II.6 stretch split); a catacomb gallery that silts, caves in or is sealed stays in its complex's extent and extentFloorM2. Own lottery: drawn at the engine's decline step after the fabric pool (under.fade) at the underground's rate, never in the fabric pool, never counted against a district's fabric cap, never in the pool's persistence order (BCR-6; V6 §3.5.2); a lived void whose last access it seals is vacated in the same batch (V6 §3.18.1 (4)).

At an epoch: Foundations.apply (under.extend's first act; 3.5.0 At an epoch; returns FoundationsResult for V06's re-homing; a catacomb node a new footing refuses records blockedBy foundation at the next growth); SewerStrategy.derive at the first sewers epoch: U-NET whole (N0-N12) over current ways as the epoch's mutation instead of extend (part 0 laid on the sewer's empty part, N3a honoured, every existing entity kept never re-derived, N8 connects R's plots, new runs join EpochScope.elements, U-ACCESS (a)'s overlap test over them in the same commit (a run crossing a sealed void opens it, cause overlap, event the epoch's seq); V06 reports under.featureOn; sewer-front dwellings follow via the crowding hook); SewerStrategy.extend(doc, epoch) at every later epoch (grow-by-stage: after the new stage's S11): N1-N6 over current ways with N3a, every node under an open existing run a root of cost 0 beside the outfalls, existing runs never re-derived, a tree path over an edge under a closed run reopens that run (regrowth-first, II.6) before any new run, new inverts fall into their receiver's, N8 for new plots only, then (a)'s overlap test for new runs; wall drops over EpochScope.levelled: each existing run crossing a RetainingWall the epoch made or re-derived takes N6's two vertices and N7 re-lays the connected network's knots, plan unchanged; ArchVaults.reconcile(doc, EpochScope.raised, epoch) in the epoch's commit (lays arch vaults of vault spans of a raised way the epoch founded or repaired, collapses those whose span or bounding support reads ruined or cleared or V06 breached or dismantled, deletes those of a removed raised way with links and accesses; new chambers join EpochScope.elements).

At a village rung the maintenance mode makes U-FADE, the foundation rule, the arch-vault reconcile and the undercity's re-read the only changes an inherited system sees (nothing grows, nothing new laid); the access pass still tests caverns, ruins, openings and village workings. CatacombGrowth.grow at an epoch (after the sewer's extension): each complex's ratchet step bounded by opts.capM2[id] (V06's per-epoch cap; without opts max(extent x ((1 + growthCapShare)^years - 1), growthFloorM2)), every complex but opts.primary held by the rank cap, plague burials x plagueNeedFactor and opts.deaths added to need never to cap; each new gallery joins EpochScope.elements and runs (a)'s overlap test and (c)'s crypt join for a church whose crypt it first reaches (V6 §3.18.3 (6)); a complex it founds lays its entrance stair and runs V01's opening pass over that entrance. QuarryWorkings.extend after the catacombs' growth (3.5.3), each commit with its overlap test and mine breach; workedOut read each epoch. UndercityEpoch.reread (under.undercity, 30; then F6 over clusters under.access made accessible this epoch): II.7.5 (5)'s size re-read past hysteresis; a shrinking neighbourhood vacates plots farthest (walkway distance) from its core first; a new neighbourhood opens only in free capacity and only in an accessible cluster; when disorder < clearanceDisorder each neighbourhood draws clearance at 1 - (1 - clearancePerYear)^years on epoch.transform keyed by its lineage, at most one clearUndercity per epoch, address order.

Access at an epoch: under.access runs AccessPass.run(doc, scope): each building the epoch builds, or gives a basement, over a cavern or ruin element draws (d)'s dig draw; the excavation reading recomputed; a cluster that became accessible takes F6's new dwellings filled by V06's relocation of the district's poorest-band ground households (V6 §3.18.1 (4)), never by S7b (6) (whose allocation at an epoch is the crowding hook's alone and runs before this pass); one that turned unexcavated (its last access sealed, bricked or deleted) vacates its dwellings and undercity plots by II.7.3's vacancy rules as fates of the epoch. The crowding hook (II.7.3 (c); V6 §3.6 (1)) sends its households through S7b (6)'s underground allocation at the epoch (BCR-V6-28 (c)) at growth before under.access: U-FRONT places them on lived runs first, then reopened ones (only where Features.sewers is on), then in the free capacity of void clusters accessible before this pass (F6); new households part of the epoch's target; F6's new dwellings in a cluster the pass opens take relocated households only, so ground, underground and sky households equal the target (T-V4-72 (f)).

Access closures: an access point's own state changes only with its host at the epoch or edit changing the host: a basement access whose building's use turns to a class whose undergroundAccess.prob is 0 at its band becomes bricked (stored, cause convert:<use op>); one whose building is demolished or whose basement is removed is deleted with its host (§2.8); a street grating or stair whose ground host is re-hosted by pointLocate onto ground II.7.3 does not admit becomes bricked; an access whose ground host a landfall covers (its ground point in a member of a fallen_island decoration: covered way, plot, land use or reservation; V05 §3.16 (4)-(5)) - grating, street stair, public opening, catacomb stair - becomes bricked, cause convert:fallIsland, until the batch in which that host leaves its fallen_island decoration (whichever op ends its cover, at an epoch or by hand; V6 §3.5.2), when it returns to open (locked where knownTo secret); a basement or dig access whose building the landfall demolishes is deleted with its host; a secret access whose building's concealed use relocates stays, locked, knownTo unchanged; the collapsed and element-sealed readings stay II.6's derived ones.

Opening places after generation: V01's opening pass (V1-3.7.1) runs inside every commit that creates, removes or re-kinds an access it selects (a public opening of source opening and role access, or a catacomb entrance stair), over those only, and at a T6 over every selected access (generation T6; the T6 of the tail after a re-derivation incl. 4.3's adjust and switch rows); at an epoch the last step of AccessPass.run with a scope and of CatacombGrowth.grow when it lays a new entrance; in an edit: delete of such an access, setAttr of its kind or role, placeAccess making a public opening, delete of a gallery or chamber carrying a selected access, a regenerate of a cavern, ruin or quarry system (removes old openings with elements, re-runs (e) over regenerated candidates keyed by new lineages, recomputes excavation, then the pass), a dwelling declaration's closure whose second or third rung makes a public opening, or the re-derivation an editTable or editPreset of V01's stage-2 switch fabric.extensionWeight makes (raised above 0 places made; lowered to 0 none made and old ones retired by §6.3 carry-over); a made access gains its HoodPlace named on naming by V1-2.8's key in the same commit; a removed one or one re-kinded out (role light) tombstones its place (V1-2.7); a kind changed within the selection re-derives the place's subtype; each a fate; a state change changes the place's symbol, never the place; the pass runs only while @plat/hood's local-place step is registered and runs (fabric.extensionWeight > 0); registration is V4 §8's registry lookup; with either missing no opening place is made and their count reported (3.11).

Failure ladder table: U-NET outfalls (no admitted candidate -> moat -> one field outfall; reported 'sewers discharge to the town ditch / a cess field'); U-NET runs (crown > coverMaxCm -> re-route <= 3 -> truncate to a local root -> gutters and pits; F-NET counts, unsewered ha); U-NET drains (head too deep -> drain dropped, plot unconnected); U-FORECAST vs built (capacity missed -> S10b reconcile, F-SITING); U-FRONT plots (sample under excluded ground -> F-UNDER); U-SYS (no admissible ground in the band -> smaller extent -> system omitted, F-VOID); U-FRONT, U-CITY (households unseated -> crowdCap -> other underground allocations -> T8, never a ground re-placement by these stages); U-CITY (void, core, lifeline missing -> C1's test: not a candidate -> fewer -> none, F-VOID, never under require); U-SYS ruin too like the town (next culture rows <= 3 -> axis turned 30 deg -> kept, W_RUIN_SIMILAR); catacomb (face failing a gate -> next face; growth blocked -> stagnation); forced vaults (ground refuses shallow grid -> floor steps below surfaceClearCm, grid grows again); U-ACCESS and U-LINK (a link end with no admissible vertex -> link skipped, counted); L5 (missing basement access, connector or outlet -> next rung -> cellar chamber always, flooded on wet ground W_SUBTERRANEAN_WET); T8 (ground capacity short -> vacant stock -> occupied stock to capacity -> reported, counted); U-DIG (basement, route or stage missing -> nearest lawful form or refusal F-EDIT §7.3 item 9 (e); in a dwelling closure's first rung a refused building passed over, then the opening rungs and the bend); ruin monument (ST0-infeasible -> clearM halved once -> no monument, W_RUIN_MONUMENT_SKIPPED); arch vault (no open face -> walled up, W_ARCH_VAULT_NO_DOOR); terminal cistern (no yard or public ground -> shrink 10 % steps to 150 m2 -> skipped, W_TERMINAL_CISTERN_SKIPPED); wall crossing (fall beyond minGradient -> the drop; climbing run by the coverMaxCm ladder); quarry at an epoch (cells run out before dV -> rest from the surface quarry, unmet m3); ruin source removed (system kept, source.ref cleared, W_RUIN_SOURCE_REMOVED); Foundations.apply (new footing over a lived void floor -> floor collapsed, dwellings vacated and returned for V06's re-homing, never a discard; under.collapsedByFoundation); opening pass (@plat/hood unregistered or fabric.extensionWeight 0 -> no opening place, underground kept whole; unregistered: first tail run after registration makes them (declared shift §13.3); switched off: made at the T6 of the re-derivation raising the switch; count of unplaced openings with cause).

Determinism: every draw on an existing concern keyed by stage id, entity key and salt: pit connection (sewer, plot); systems' existence and each source's chance (sewer, kind and source); ruin existence (sewer, its source or town root), culture row and shared axis, axis jitter, significance, extent, age (sewer, the ruin), decay survival (sewer, the element); burial-face chance (sewer, the face); cavern meander and hall vertices (sewer, path start cell); tube count, fissure count, fissure gallery width and headroom (sewer, cavern system, gallery); undercity existence (sewer, settlement, undercity; overlap shaft (sewer, element pair); opening (sewer, candidate element, opening kind); dig (sewer in U-ACCESS, building, salt void kind); crypt join (sewer, church and complex source, no epoch component); ruin magic lights (sewer, chamber); monument ST1 draws (sewer, ruin system, chamber plan coordinate, 'tiers/0' then 'tiers/1', attempt index on an ST6 retry), tier decay (sewer, chamber key, 'tiers/decay', tier index), colonnade survival (sewer, chamber key, 'colonnade', row index); underground plots and buildings (plot.*, siting, siteplan, heights keyed from pseudo-district or neighbourhood); door-light sides (pin.light); fade and clearance (epoch.transform); T8 placements (siting, receiving district); names (naming); no new concern; a span's use is the base's draw on its raised-way stream (BCR-45), V04 draws nothing for an arch vault or terminal cistern (arch-vault set independent of district opening order, T-V4-70); at an epoch keys take the epoch component except the dig draw, the catacomb source draw, each public opening and overlap shaft draw, and the crypt join (fixed by key, never re-drawn; ST-16; J-V6.52, T-V6-34) - a building's dig draw at the epoch that builds it equals a regeneration's (prefix-stable), a face refused at TOWN compares the same draw against CITY's chance later; QuarryWorkings.extend and SewerStrategy.derive at an epoch draw nothing new but pit draws; the hood line, Foundations.apply, village-working test and buried terrace steps draw nothing; opening pass names are V01's draws on naming (V1-2.8); every loop in address order, ties by address or index, tail serial on one worker, integer cm, transcendentals via dmath (§6.5); a New random on a system, run or neighbourhood advances its reroll and writes only its own part, but for its links' far ends (§3.4), the carve's split parts, and on a cavern, ruin or quarry system V01's opening places over openings (e) makes and removes; a New random on the catacomb system removes nothing.

Declarations (points in, shape out; item 101 (i)): drawTunnel (sewer, no system): two points, optional kind; dry run: where both points lie within outfall.linkM of ways U-NET's tree search between the nearest graph nodes (N3's costs), else the straight segment; an end within 2 m of a run joins it (a junction); kind when not given a main where either end lies within outfall.linkM of a way else a drain; profile by kind and preset; invert by N7 from the lower end; navigable derived; overlap test at commit; handles four to eight route vertices and the ends. drawTunnel with a system (a gallery): catacomb or quarry gallery an L-route on its system's grid axis; ruin gallery an L-route on the ruin's axisDeg; any other a straight segment; floor from the nearer existing element else the row's depth range middle (ruin: g(p)). drawChamber: one point and a size or three+ points: a rounded rectangle aligned with the nearest gallery (ruin: a right-angled rectangle on the ruin's axis, kind room unless given) or the polygon; floor from the nearest element; kind the row's first. addLink: one point on each of two elements of different parts (nearest within 5 m), via by (b)'s floor rule, kind open unless given, cause edit. placeAccess: one ground point: the element nearest below within 10 m in plan on any part (shallowest first); kind by the drop and host: on public ground II.7.3's neighbourhood kinds (street stair within stairMaxDepthCm, a well shaft in a yard or square, else a shaft; a grating of role air when asked); in a building the basement kinds (II.7.3 (3)); role access, cause edit; asked for a public opening's kind (sinkhole, mouth, collapsed_shaft, ruin_entrance) makes that opening at the nearest candidate of that kind within 10 m whatever its draw gave (source opening, role access, cause {edit, system, event}, knownTo by (e)'s rule, V01's opening pass in the same commit); no such candidate -> refused, nearest candidate offered; over an unexcavated cluster it is the user's excavation (dry run lists every cluster becoming accessible transitively; dwellings come at the next Re-derive from S7b or next epoch). addUndergroundAccess (building click): the closure (3.8); with no target grouped before a dwelling declaration on an unexcavated cluster (V9 §4.17.4 Use another building) its target by 3.8's grouped-access rule. A raised way added (base T4 road raised or aqueduct class): the base's spans with use by BCR-45; V04's arch vaults and, for an aqueduct with a cistern terminal, its terminal cistern as fates in the same dry run.

Two reads every points form shares: a ground point is read on ground part 0 (on a raised deck resolves to the ground beneath; a click on the sky layer resolves to ground part 0 beneath, no island building or face a host; inside a raised-way pier's footprint moves to the nearest free part-0 point, reported); an access from a church-class building to a catacomb element (placeAccess in it or addUndergroundAccess naming a catacomb target) is a hand crypt join (source crypt, cause {crypt, system, event}, head in the crypt); a building without Basement.crypt refused with the fix offered (setAttr(basement) on basement/crypt/ring, V03 §4.2). A dry run shows the derived shape as a ghost with fates; accepted, stored resolved, no later derivation moves it (declared means held, §7.2; N3a); showing the underground layer makes it the active layer until the user picks another (V09's control); while active T4 draws a tunnel or link, T6 a chamber or access, T9 every attribute; no thirteenth tool (§13.2).

chamber kind (ChamberKind; archVault only by the arch source, setAttr to or from it refused), ceilingCm >= 200, elevationCm in the depth range, knownTo -> plots under it re-capped (II.7.5), a lowered ceiling re-fits buildings by S11's mutator and cuts a monument's tiers; J-V4.4: chose the tree as a multi-source shortest-path search from the admitted outfalls over the way graph (D8 itself for `drainage-lines`) over a network optimisation, because it is deterministic, O(E log V), and reproduces the downhill-to-the-nearest-outlet shape

J-V4.5: chose tunnel selection by accumulated served area against per-preset thresholds, with the downstream closure, over per-street rules, because the served area is what sizes a sewer (II.7.2's law) and so one quantity decides existence and size
J-V4.6: chose one leaves-to-root invert pass with a re-route, then truncate, ladder over lowering the terrain, because the owner's town never trenches and every run must fall

J-V4.7: chose outfalls from S1's drainage outlets, admitted downstream of the harbour and the mills, with the town moat and then a cess field as fallbacks, over a fixed river outfall, because a town may lie on the sea, a lake or dry ground and historically discharged to its ditch when it had nothing better

J-V4.8: chose logical house connections (`serves`) over drawn house drains, and drains only for the priority institutions, because thousands of stub tunnels would cost arena edges and draw clutter for a fact the reader already gives

J-V4.10: chose navigable-preset passages at the mains' closest approaches over random cross-links, because loops where mains nearly meet read as a planned fantasy network and stay deterministic

J-V4.11: chose the network's own gratings at a manhole spacing on public ground and mouths at outfalls and culvert inlets, over access only where people live, because a maintained sewer has openings and the undercity's lifelines and the connection graph need them
J-V4.12: chose `Way.flowToward` as a derived reading over a stored field, because no stage produced it and a stored copy would go stale after every terrain edit

level reading: the levels V02's storeyRange gives each wing (solid none; ground wing [0, floors-1]; stacked from the level above its host); s0(w) its first level.
ground(b): level 0 when some storeyed wing stands on no other wing, absent otherwise (every ground wing solid); every rule meaning the real ground reads it, never 'storey 0'.
stair-entered (crypt): ground(b) exists and a storeyed ground-standing wing's ring shares area with the crypt's vault; entered by crypt stairs, else from the basement.
vault (of a crypt): Basement.crypt.ring with its capped bays = the step-2 ring (never moved by the rank), or the author's ring where edited.
capped bays: the crypt's step-2 ring less the trimmed Basement.crypt.ring, inside Basement.ring; planned as one undercroft room.

principal crypt: the cathedral building's (largest ring among several, ties address), else the always building's with the largest ring, else none; every other crypt capped at crypt.rankShare x its area.
crypt-only basement: a basement whose Basement.ring is the crypt's ring, floors 1, access core with crypt stairs as cores (or external via basementDoor(b) where ground(b) absent).

door side / door point / span: a Basement.ring side at least two moduleCm long; its midpoint, or on a church with ground(b) the nearest point whose two-module span shares no length with the crypt's vault.

outline / door part / admissible point (stackAccessDoor): the edge of the ground-standing wings' union; a maximal outline stretch of a wing side >= two moduleCm; a point >= one moduleCm from each end whose span clears stair 0's approach strip by one moduleCm.
solidMonument: the information (no failure) that a building has no storeyed wing: no level at or above the ground and no room there.

roof terrace T(x), walkable terrace, roof level: T(x) = ring(x) minus the rings of wings on x for a flat-roofed x; walkable when a flight head, terrace exit or landing/terrace door reaches it; a roof level = storeyRange(x)[1] + 1 with no rooms.
landing door, terrace exit, terrace door, seating exit, stack root: the S6 joins of a stacked wing and O2's further tree roots.

outsideCm / exposure: the surface sampled door.mainCm outward from a wall's midpoint via levelledGroundCm (far side of a retaining wall, deck surface, water, a lower wing's roof); exposure of a basement wall = baseCm of the ground wing above less outsideCm.
stoop: the uncapped outside flight of steps = ceil(delta/riserCm) at a main entrance whose floor lies more than riserCm above its ground and meets no level.
walk-out (wall, fall) and tomb door: basementDoor(b)'s rules 1 (retaining wall), 3 (lowest outside ground) and 2 (outside stair to a door at the basement floor where ground(b) is absent).
head (of a way down): the plan's anchored end of an AccessPoint the building hosts (AccessHead), with host room, opening, through-ring; a head of storey null lies on no storey (an outside door).
structural faces: rooms of roles stair, stack, shaft, column that tile the storey's extents, never allocated or furnished; stack and a shaft's through-ring never labelled or entered.

main slot / half / claimed storey / vacant programme / unit floor: the template's first required structure (else first); works/shop/both from Use.branchOf; a storey a hard non-unit room's class claims; the programme of a building with no use and no household; the per-form minimum unit area.
exchange class: non-anchored rooms of a storey sharing scope, unit, maxDoors, hub-ness and door kind whose roles fit every member piece; plan.roles permutes roles inside it.
grade face: a host chamber's side V04 marks open to ground part 0 (an arch vault's open face, a bridge approach's or street vault's open arch), planned as an exterior wall at grade.

service region R, run, trunk, drop, field outfall, culvert: R = ground districts not hinterland, underground or undercity; a run = one Tunnel cut at degree != 2 nodes, kind and way changes, outfalls; a trunk = a run reaching trunkHa; a drop = a steep segment between two wall-face knots in one run; a field outfall = the cess field of a dry town; a culvert = a covered brook of catchment >= culvertCatchHa.

within reach / foundation obstacle / pillar: an element's plan band meets an obstacle's footprint grown by foundationClearM and its top lies above the obstacle's bottom; obstacles = raised-way piers, retaining-wall footings, buried aqueduct stretches; a pillar = a footing standing in an older chamber covered < collapseShare.

maintenance mode: an inherited system at a village rung re-derives its own part from kept elements, lays nothing new, never grows; U-FADE, foundations, arch-vault reconcile and undercity re-read are its only changes.

hood line: the tail's rules in a standalone neighbourhood (Recipe.product 'hood'): the below-TOWN set plus one catacomb at TOWN's rules on the hood's own faces; U-FORECAST after the one-district allocation.
cluster / excavation reading / accessible / unexcavated: a connected component of a part's open galleries and chambers; the derived reading whether the connection graph joins it to the surface.

burial face / primary / stagnant / closed face / ratchet / quarry ossuary / charnel vault: a catacomb's source (churchyard, cemetery, network ground, monastery burial yard); the complex serving the most burials; need beyond laid capacity with no admissible frontier; a face whose use is closed or record removed; only-add growth; a worked-out quarry adopted at CITY+; a dug ossuary chamber below TOWN.
lived: a run, system or cluster carrying plots or within litReachM of one; lit only when lived.

working / surface quarry / worked out: a 4-connected group of taken stone or ore cells as one workings chamber; §4.9's quarry land use without a source; a reading (mine use closed, chain inactive, stone working outside the epoch that laid it).

arch vault / span / terminal cistern: an at-grade archVault chamber in a raised way's vault span keyed by its pier pair; the under-deck span between two piers (use open or vault, base's eager fact); an aqueduct's cistern terminal chamber under its conduit house's yard.

ruin / culture row / significance / persistence class / mausoleum / monument / colonnade row: an older civilisation's remnant plan system; its V11 plan row; shrine, palace or district extent; the survival class of an element; the necropolis's central tomb chamber; a stepped mass laid by layTiers; a line of column nodes along u.

undercity core / plaza / walkway / carve / outskirts / underground pseudo-district: a neighbourhood's main chamber (District.core); its disc ringed by a walkway; MST walkways inside chambers; the 16-gon market carved where no chamber qualifies; the sewer-front blocks linked to it (L6); the one district holding sewer-front neighbourhoods and F6's void dwellings.
overlap / mine breach / proximity link / crypt join / dig / public opening / reuse: the U-ACCESS link and access kinds, each recording its cause.
